title.zh: 卷九十四 志第七十 刑法二
title.raw: 卷九十四 志第七十 刑法二 Volume 94 Treatises 70: Punishment and Law 2

sentences.zh: 三法司曰刑部、都察院、大理寺。

translations.literal: The Three Judicial Offices were the Ministry of Punishment, the Censorate, and the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Judicial Offices comprised the Ministry of Punishment, the Censorate, and the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 刑部受天下刑名，都察院糾察，大理寺駁正。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Punishment received all penal cases under Heaven; the Censorate investigated and exposed irregularities; the Court of Judicial Review rejected and corrected rulings.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Punishment took charge of penal matters throughout the realm; the Censorate investigated misconduct; and the Court of Judicial Review reviewed and overturned improper judgments.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗曰：「凡有大獄，當面訊，防構陷鍛煉之弊。」

translations.literal: The Founder once said: "For all major cases, one must question face to face, to guard against the abuse of framing and forcing confessions through torture.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu once declared: "In every major case, the accused must be questioned in person, lest officials resort to framing suspects or torturing them into false confessions.

sentences.zh: 故其時重案多親鞫，不委法司。

translations.literal: Therefore at that time major cases were mostly personally interrogated and not entrusted to the judicial offices.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, grave cases were usually tried by the emperor himself rather than delegated to the judicial bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 洪武十四年，命刑部聽兩造之詞，議定入奏。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Hongwu, the Ministry of Punishment was ordered to hear the statements of both parties, deliberate, and memorialize the decision.
translations.idiomatic: In 1381, an order directed the Ministry of Punishment to hear both sides, reach a proposed judgment, and report it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 既奏，錄所下旨，送四輔官、諫院官、給事中覆核無異，然後覆奏行之。

translations.literal: After the memorial was submitted, the imperial rescript was recorded and sent to the four chief counselors, remonstrance officials, and supervising secretaries for re-examination; if there was no discrepancy, it was then resubmitted and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Once the memorial was in, the emperor's decision was recorded and sent to the four chief counselors, censors, and supervising secretaries for review; if they found no fault, the case was reported again and executed.

sentences.zh: 有疑獄，則四輔官封駁之。

translations.literal: If there was a doubtful case, the four chief counselors sealed and returned it for revision.
translations.idiomatic: Doubtful cases were sealed and sent back by the four chief counselors for reconsideration.

sentences.zh: 逾年，四輔官罷，乃命議獄者一歸於三法司。

translations.literal: After more than a year the four chief counselors were dismissed, and cases under deliberation were all returned to the Three Judicial Offices.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, with the four chief counselors removed from office, all criminal deliberation was entrusted once again to the Three Judicial Offices.

sentences.zh: 十六年，命刑部尚書開濟等，議定五六日旬時三審五覆之法。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Minister of Punishment Kai Ji and others were ordered to deliberate and fix the method of three trials and five reviews within five or six days per ten-day period.
translations.idiomatic: In 1383, Kai Ji, Minister of Punishment, and others were charged with establishing the schedule of three trials and five reviews every five or six days within each ten-day period.

sentences.zh: 十七年，建三法司於太平門外鐘山之陰，命之曰貫城。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, the Three Judicial Offices were built north of Bell Mountain outside the Taiping Gate, and the compound was named Guancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In 1384 the Three Judicial Offices were erected north of Bell Mountain, outside the Taiping Gate, and the compound was named Guancheng, "the Pierced City."

sentences.zh: 下敕言：「貫索七星如貫珠，環而成象名天牢。

translations.literal: An imperial edict stated: "The seven stars of Guansuo resemble strung beads, forming the image called the Celestial Prison.
translations.idiomatic: An edict explained: "The seven stars of Guansuo lie like beads on a string, forming the constellation known as the Celestial Prison.

sentences.zh: 中虛則刑平，官無邪私，故獄無囚人；

translations.literal: When its center is empty, punishments are balanced and officials are without private corruption, and therefore the prison has no inmates;
translations.idiomatic: When the constellation's center stands empty, punishments are even-handed and officials free of private corruption, and the prison holds no prisoners;

sentences.zh: 貫內空中有星或數枚者即刑繁，刑官非其人；

translations.literal: if there are one or several stars within the empty center, punishments are excessive and the penal officials are not the right men;
translations.idiomatic: if one or more stars appear within that hollow, punishments grow harsh and the magistrates are unfit for their posts;

sentences.zh: 有星而明，為貴人無罪而獄。

translations.literal: when stars are present and bright, nobles are imprisoned though guiltless.
translations.idiomatic: when stars shine there, men of rank may languish in prison though innocent.

sentences.zh: 今法天道置法司，爾諸司其各慎乃事，法天道行之，令貫索中虛，庶不負朕肇建之意。」

translations.literal: Now, in setting up judicial offices in accord with Heaven's Way, you various offices must each be careful in your duties and act in accord with Heaven's Way, so that Guansuo's center may be empty and you may not betray my purpose in founding this institution."
translations.idiomatic: In establishing these courts to mirror Heaven's Way, each of you must discharge your duties with care, so that Guansuo's center may stand empty and you fulfill the intent with which I founded them.

sentences.zh: 又諭法司官：「佈政、按察司所擬刑名，其間人命重獄，具奏轉達刑部、都察院參考，大理寺詳擬。

translations.literal: He also instructed the judicial officials: "The penal cases proposed by provincial administration and surveillance commissioners, among which are capital cases involving life, shall all be memorialized and forwarded to the Ministry of Punishment and Censorate for reference, and the Court of Judicial Review shall deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: He further told the judicial officers: "Capital cases and other grave penalties proposed by provincial administration and surveillance commissioners must be reported upward to the Ministry of Punishment and the Censorate for consultation, with the Court of Judicial Review conducting a detailed review.

sentences.zh: 著為令。」

translations.literal: This is established as an ordinance."
translations.idiomatic: Let this be enacted as a standing regulation."

sentences.zh: 刑部有十三清吏司，治各布政司刑名，而陵衛、王府、公侯伯府、在京諸曹及兩京州郡，亦分隸之。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Punishment had thirteen bureaus of clerks, each handling penal cases of a provincial administration commission, while mausoleums, princely establishments, noble mansions, capital offices, and the two capitals' prefectures and districts were also apportioned among them.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry was divided into thirteen clerical bureaus, each overseeing the penal docket of a provincial administration commission; imperial tombs, princely households, noble mansions, metropolitan agencies, and the prefectures and districts of the two capitals fell under their jurisdiction as well.

sentences.zh: 按察名提刑，蓋在外之法司也，參以副使、僉事，分治各府縣事。

translations.literal: The surveillance commission was called the office for raising penalties, being in effect the judicial office outside the capital; assistant commissioners and assistant surveillance commissioners participated, each administering the affairs of the various prefectures and districts.
translations.idiomatic: The surveillance commission, styled the office for raising penalties, served as the provincial judiciary; vice commissioners and surveillance commissioners shared its work, each supervising the cases of his circuit of prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 京師自笞以上罪，悉由部議。

translations.literal: In the capital, punishments from beating with the light bamboo stick upward were all decided by the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Within the capital, every penalty from the light bamboo beating upward was adjudicated by the ministry alone.

sentences.zh: 洪武初決獄，笞五十者縣決之，杖八十者州決之，一百者府決之，徒以上具獄送行省，移駁繁而賄賂行。

translations.literal: In the early years of Hongwu, when deciding cases, those liable to fifty blows of the light bamboo were decided by the county, eighty blows by the prefecture, one hundred by the prefectural administration, and penal servitude and above were sent with full records to the provincial administration commission; repeated review grew cumbersome and bribery flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongwu reign, counties decided cases up to fifty blows of the light bamboo, prefectures up to eighty, and the prefectural administration up to one hundred; penal servitude and heavier penalties required full dossiers sent to the provincial commission. Endless rehearings bred delay and bribery.

sentences.zh: 乃命中書省御史臺詳讞，改月報為季報，以季報之數，類為歲報。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Secretariat and the Censorate were ordered to review judgments in detail, monthly reports were changed to quarterly reports, and the quarterly figures were classified into annual reports.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered the Secretariat and Censorate to review judgments carefully, replaced monthly returns with quarterly ones, and rolled the quarterly totals into annual reports.

sentences.zh: 凡府州縣輕重獄囚，依律決斷。

translations.literal: All serious and light prisoners in prefectures, departments, and counties were decided according to the code.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures, departments, and counties were to decide all prisoners, grave or minor, strictly according to statute.

sentences.zh: 違枉者，御史、按察司糾劾。

translations.literal: Those who violated or distorted the law were impeached by censors and surveillance commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who misapplied or perverted the law were impeached by censors and surveillance commissioners.

sentences.zh: 至二十六年定制，布政司及直隸府州縣，笞杖就決；

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year a fixed system was established: for provincial administration commissions and directly administered prefectures, departments, and counties, bamboo punishments were decided on the spot;
translations.idiomatic: In 1393 a permanent rule was laid down: provincial administration commissions and directly governed prefectures, departments, and counties could impose bamboo punishments locally;

sentences.zh: 徒流、遷徙、充軍、雜犯死罪解部，審錄行下，具死囚所坐罪名上部詳議如律者，大理寺擬覆平允，監收侯決。

translations.literal: penal servitude, exile, banishment, military exile, miscellaneous offenses, and death sentences were sent to the ministry; after review and transmission downward, when death-row convicts and their crimes were reported to the ministry and deliberated in accordance with the code, the Court of Judicial Review would review and confirm fairness, take them into custody, and await execution.
translations.idiomatic: penal servitude, exile, banishment, military exile, miscellaneous capital offenses, and death sentences went to the ministry. After review, death-row prisoners whose convictions matched the code were re-examined by the Court of Judicial Review, held in custody, and kept pending execution.

sentences.zh: 其決不待時重囚，報可，即奏遣官往決之。

translations.literal: For heavy prisoners whose execution could not await the season, once approved they were at once memorialized and officials were dispatched to carry out the sentence.
translations.idiomatic: Capital prisoners whose sentences could not wait for the regular season, once approved, were reported immediately and officers were sent to execute the sentence.

sentences.zh: 情詞不明或失出入者，大理寺駁回改正，再問駁至三，改擬不當，將當該官吏奏問，謂之照駁。

translations.literal: If the facts were unclear or there was error in severity or leniency, the Court of Judicial Review returned the case for correction; after three returns and revisions still improper, the responsible officials were memorialized and questioned—this was called reflective rejection.
translations.idiomatic: If facts were unclear or the sentence too harsh or too lenient, the Court of Judicial Review sent the case back for correction. After three such returns, if the revision was still wrong, the responsible officials were reported to the throne—this was called reflective rejection.

sentences.zh: 若亭疑讞決，而囚有番異，則改調隔別衙門問擬。

translations.literal: If after doubtful deliberation and judgment the prisoner still disputed the verdict, the case was transferred for rehearing to a separate yamen.
translations.idiomatic: When deliberation left doubt and the prisoner still contested the verdict, the case was reassigned to another office for a fresh hearing.

sentences.zh: 二次番異不服，則具奏，會九卿鞫之，謂之圓審。

translations.literal: After a second dispute and refusal to accept the verdict, a memorial was submitted and the Nine Ministers jointly interrogated—this was called the round review.
translations.idiomatic: If the prisoner disputed the verdict a second time, the case was memorialized and the Nine Ministers jointly tried it—the round review.

sentences.zh: 至三四訊不服，而後請旨決焉。

translations.literal: Only after three or four interrogations without submission would imperial decision be requested.
translations.idiomatic: Only after three or four hearings without submission would the case be referred to the emperor for final decision.

sentences.zh: 正統四年，稍更直省決遣之制，徒流就彼決遣，死罪以聞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengtong the system for deciding and dispatching cases in directly administered provinces was slightly altered: penal servitude and exile were decided and dispatched there, and death sentences were reported.
translations.idiomatic: In 1439 the rules for directly governed provinces were slightly revised: penal servitude and exile could be decided and executed locally, while death sentences had to be reported to the center.

sentences.zh: 成化五年，南大理評事張鈺言：「南京法司多用嚴刑，迫囚誣服，其被糾者亦止改正而無罪，甚非律意。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chenghua, Nanjing Court of Judicial Review evaluating official Zhang Yu said: "The Nanjing judicial offices often use harsh torture, forcing prisoners to confess falsely; those impeached are only corrected without being found innocent—this greatly departs from the intent of the code.
translations.idiomatic: In 1469 Zhang Yu, an evaluating official at the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review, protested that Nanjing's judicial offices routinely tortured prisoners into false confessions and that impeached officials merely revised judgments without exonerating the innocent—conduct far from the spirit of the law.

sentences.zh: 乃詔申大理寺參問刑部之制。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued reaffirming the Court of Judicial Review's system of joint inquiry with the Ministry of Punishment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict thereupon reaffirmed the Court of Judicial Review's practice of joint inquiry with the Ministry of Punishment.

sentences.zh: 弘治十七年，刑部主事硃瑬言：「部囚送大理，第當駁正，不當用刑。」

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Hongzhi, Ministry of Punishment registrar Zhu Rong said: "When ministry prisoners are sent to the Court of Judicial Review, it should only reject and correct; it should not apply torture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1504 Zhu Rong, a registrar in the Ministry of Punishment, argued that prisoners sent from the ministry to the Court of Judicial Review should be corrected on the merits alone, not subjected to torture.

sentences.zh: 大理卿楊守隨言：「刑具永樂間設，不可廢。」

translations.literal: Court of Judicial Review director Yang Shousui said: "Instruments of torture were established in the Yongle period and cannot be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: Director Yang Shousui of the Court of Judicial Review replied that torture implements introduced in the Yongle reign could not be abolished.

sentences.zh: 帝是其言。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his statement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sided with Yang.

sentences.zh: 會官審錄之例，定於洪武三十年。

translations.literal: The precedent for joint official review of records was fixed in the thirtieth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: The practice of joint official review of prisoners was established in 1397.

sentences.zh: 初制，有大獄必面訊。

translations.literal: Under the initial system, major cases had to be interrogated in person.
translations.idiomatic: Under the original rule, major cases required personal interrogation by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 十四年，命法司論囚，擬律以奏，從翰林院、給事中及春坊正字、司直郎會議平允，然後覆奏論決。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, judicial offices were ordered to discuss prisoners, propose punishments according to the code and memorialize; the Hanlin Academy, supervising secretaries, and senior secretaries and readers of the Eastern Palace would jointly discuss fairness, and then the case would be resubmitted for judgment and decision.
translations.idiomatic: In 1381 judicial offices were to deliberate on prisoners, propose sentences under the code, and memorialize; Hanlin academicians, supervising secretaries, and Eastern Palace readers would confer on fairness before the verdict went back to the throne.

sentences.zh: 至是置政平、訟理二幡，審諭罪囚。

translations.literal: At this time the banners "Government at Peace" and "Litigation Resolved" were set up to announce sentences to guilty prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the banners "Government at Peace" and "Litigation Resolved" were erected to proclaim sentences to convicted prisoners.

sentences.zh: 諭刑部曰：「自今論囚，惟武臣、死罪，朕親審之，餘俱以所犯奏。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Punishment was instructed: "From now on in judging prisoners, only military officials and death sentences shall I personally try; for all others report the offense committed.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry was told: "Henceforth I shall personally try only military offenders and capital cases; report all other offenses as charged.

sentences.zh: 然後引至承天門外，命行人持訟理幡，傳旨諭之；

translations.literal: Then they were led outside the Chengtian Gate, and runners bearing the Litigation Resolved banner transmitted the imperial words and announced the sentence;
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners were then led outside the Chengtian Gate, where runners with the Litigation Resolved banner conveyed the imperial message and pronounced sentence;

sentences.zh: 其無罪應釋者，持政平幡，宣德意遣之。」

translations.literal: those who should be released as innocent were sent away under the Government at Peace banner, proclaiming the imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: those to be released as innocent were dismissed under the Government at Peace banner, proclaiming imperial mercy.

sentences.zh: 繼令五軍都督府、六部、都察院、六科、通政司、詹事府，間及駙馬雜聽之，錄冤者以狀聞，無冤者實犯死罪以下悉論如律，諸雜犯準贖。

translations.literal: Subsequently the Five Military Commissions, Six Ministries, Censorate, Six Offices of Scrutiny, Office of Transmission, and Grand Secretariat were also intermittently ordered to sit in and hear cases, together with sons-in-law of the emperor; those recording wrongful convictions reported by memorial, while the guiltless and those whose actual offense was below death were all judged according to the code, and miscellaneous offenses were ransomed as permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Five Military Commissions, Six Ministries, Censorate, Six Offices of Scrutiny, Office of Transmission, and Grand Secretariat—and sometimes imperial sons-in-law—were also summoned to hear cases. Wrongful convictions were memorialized; the innocent and those whose true offense fell short of death were sentenced under the code; miscellaneous offenses were commuted by ransom as allowed.

sentences.zh: 永樂七年，令大理寺官引法司囚犯赴承天門外，行人持節傳旨，會同府、部、通政司、六科等官審錄，如洪武制。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongle, Court of Judicial Review officials were ordered to lead judicial prisoners outside the Chengtian Gate; runners bore credentials to transmit the edict, and officials of the prefecture, ministries, Office of Transmission, Six Offices, and others jointly reviewed records as under the Hongwu system.
translations.idiomatic: In 1409 Court of Judicial Review officials led prisoners from the judicial offices outside the Chengtian Gate; runners carried credentials to announce the edict, and officials from the capital administration, ministries, Office of Transmission, Six Offices, and other agencies jointly reviewed the records as in the Hongwu system.

sentences.zh: 十七年，令在外死罪重囚，悉赴京師審錄。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, all heavy death-row prisoners outside the capital were ordered to be brought to the capital for joint review.
translations.idiomatic: In 1419 all serious death-row prisoners in the provinces were ordered brought to the capital for joint review.

sentences.zh: 仁宗特命內閣學士會審重囚，可疑者再問。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong specially ordered Grand Secretariat academicians to join in reviewing heavy prisoners; doubtful cases were tried again.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong specially ordered Grand Secretariat academicians to sit with others in reviewing capital cases; doubtful cases were reheard.

sentences.zh: 宣德三年奏重囚，帝令多官覆閱之，曰：「古者斷獄，必訊於三公九卿，所以合至公，重民命。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuande, when heavy prisoners were memorialized, the emperor ordered many officials to re-examine them, saying: "In antiquity, when judging cases, inquiry was made of the Three Dukes and Nine Ministers, thereby combining utmost fairness and valuing the people's lives.
translations.idiomatic: In 1428, reviewing capital cases, the Xuande Emperor ordered many officials to re-examine them, saying: "In antiquity capital trials required consultation with the Three Dukes and Nine Ministers, uniting supreme fairness with reverence for human life.

sentences.zh: 卿等往同覆審，毋致枉死。」

translations.literal: You are to go and jointly re-examine; do not cause wrongful death.
translations.idiomatic: Go together and review again—do not let the innocent die.

sentences.zh: 英國公張輔等還奏，訴枉者五十六人，重命法司勘實，因切戒焉。

translations.literal: The Duke of Ying Zhang Fu and others returned and reported that fifty-six persons pleaded wrongful conviction; the emperor again ordered the judicial offices to verify the facts and sternly admonished them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fu, Duke of Ying, and the others reported back that fifty-six prisoners claimed wrongful conviction. The emperor ordered the judicial offices to verify the facts and sharply rebuked them.

sentences.zh: 天順三年，令每歲霜降後，三法司同公、侯、伯會審重囚，謂之朝審。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianshun, after each year's Frost's Descent, the Three Judicial Offices together with dukes, marquises, and earls jointly reviewed heavy prisoners—this was called the Court Review.
translations.idiomatic: In 1459 an order required that after Frost's Descent each year the Three Judicial Offices, together with dukes, marquises, and earls, jointly review capital prisoners—the Court Review.

sentences.zh: 歷朝遂遵行之。

translations.literal: Succeeding dynasties thereafter followed the practice.
translations.idiomatic: Later reigns kept the practice.

sentences.zh: 成化十七年，命司禮太監一員會同三法司堂上官，於大理寺審錄，謂之大審。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Chenghua, one director of ceremonial from the Directorate of Ceremonial was ordered to join the senior officials of the Three Judicial Offices at the Court of Judicial Review in reviewing records—this was called the Grand Review.
translations.idiomatic: In 1481 one eunuch director of ceremonial was ordered to sit with the chief officers of the Three Judicial Offices at the Court of Judicial Review for the Grand Review.

sentences.zh: 南京則命內守備行之。

translations.literal: At Nanjing the inner palace superintendent was ordered to conduct it.
translations.idiomatic: At Nanjing the inner palace superintendent conducted it.

sentences.zh: 自此定例，每五年輒大審。

translations.literal: From this a fixed precedent was established: every five years a Grand Review was held.
translations.idiomatic: This became fixed precedent: a Grand Review every five years.

sentences.zh: 初，成祖定熱審之例，英宗特行朝審，至是復有大審，所矜疑放遣，嘗倍於熱審時。

translations.literal: Initially Emperor Chengzu established the precedent for Summer Review; Emperor Yingzong specially instituted the Court Review; by this time there was again the Grand Review, and those released on doubtful grounds often doubled the number at Summer Review.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Chengzu had first established the Summer Review; Emperor Yingzong added the Court Review; now the Grand Review as well often freed twice as many prisoners on grounds of doubt as the Summer Review.

sentences.zh: 內閣之與審也，自憲宗罷，至隆慶元年，高拱復行之。

translations.literal: As for the Grand Secretariat joining in review, after it ceased under Emperor Xianzong, Gao Gong revived it in the first year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Secretariat's participation in review lapsed under Emperor Xianzong until Gao Gong restored it in 1567.

sentences.zh: 故事，朝審吏部尚書秉筆，時拱適兼吏部故也。

translations.literal: By precedent the Minister of Personnel held the brush at the Court Review; at that time Gao Gong happened also to hold the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: By custom the Minister of Personnel presided at the Court Review; Gao Gong happened to hold that ministry as well.

sentences.zh: 至萬曆二十六年朝審，吏部尚書缺，以戶部尚書楊俊民主之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Wanli, at the Court Review the Minister of Personnel was vacant, and Minister of Revenue Yang Junmin presided.
translations.idiomatic: At the 1598 Court Review the Ministry of Personnel had no incumbent, so Minister of Revenue Yang Junmin presided.

sentences.zh: 三十二年復缺，以戶部尚書趙世卿主之。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year the post was again vacant, and Minister of Revenue Zhao Shiqing presided.
translations.idiomatic: In 1604 it was vacant again, and Minister of Revenue Zhao Shiqing presided.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十五年，命首輔周延儒同三法司清理淹獄，蓋出於特旨云。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Chongzhen, the chief grand secretary Zhou Yanru was ordered together with the Three Judicial Offices to clear long-pending cases—this issued from a special edict.
translations.idiomatic: In 1642 chief grand secretary Zhou Yanru was ordered, with the Three Judicial Offices, to clear long-pending cases by special edict.

sentences.zh: 大審，自萬曆二十九年曠不舉，四十四年乃行之。

translations.literal: The Grand Review, having lapsed since the twenty-ninth year of Wanli, was held again in the forty-fourth year.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Review, omitted since 1601, was held again in 1616.

sentences.zh: 熱審始永樂二年，止決遣輕罪，命出獄聽候而已。

translations.literal: Summer Review began in the second year of Yongle; at first only light offenses were decided and released, ordered out of prison to await further disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Summer Review began in 1404, at first releasing only minor offenders from prison pending further disposition.

sentences.zh: 尋並寬及徒流以下。

translations.literal: Soon it was extended to include penal servitude and exile as well.
translations.idiomatic: Soon it was extended to penal servitude and exile.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年五、六、七月，連論三法司錄上繫囚罪狀，凡決遣二千八百餘人。

translations.literal: In the fifth, sixth, and seventh months of the second year of Xuande, the Three Judicial Offices three times memorialized the offenses of prisoners in custody; in all more than twenty-eight hundred persons were decided and released.
translations.idiomatic: In 1427, during the fifth, sixth, and seventh months of Xuande, the Three Judicial Offices three times reported prisoners in custody; more than twenty-eight hundred were released or sentenced.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，親閱法司所進繫囚罪狀，決遣千餘人，減等輸納，春審自此始。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year, the emperor personally reviewed the offense lists submitted by the judicial offices and decided and released more than a thousand persons, with commutation by payment in kind—thus Spring Review began.
translations.idiomatic: In February 1432 the emperor personally reviewed the judicial offices' lists and released more than a thousand prisoners, many with reduced sentences by payment in kind—thus began the Spring Review.

sentences.zh: 六月，又以炎暑，命自實犯死罪外，悉早發遣，且馳諭中外刑獄悉如之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, because of the heat, an order was issued that except for those guilty of capital offenses in fact, all were to be released early; and urgent edicts were sent to penal establishments throughout the empire to follow suit.
translations.idiomatic: In June, owing to the heat, he ordered that all except those actually guilty of capital crimes be released promptly, and edicts rushed to prisons everywhere to do the same.

sentences.zh: 成化時，熱審始有重罪矜疑、輕罪減等、枷號疏放諸例。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua period, Summer Review first acquired precedents for doubtful capital offenses, reduction of light sentences, and release on bond with cangue.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chenghua, Summer Review first gained precedents for leniency in capital cases, reduction of lighter sentences, and release wearing the cangue.

sentences.zh: 正德元年，掌大理寺工部尚書楊守隨言：「每歲熱審事例，行於北京而不行於南京。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde, Yang Shousui, Minister of Works acting as director of the Court of Judicial Review, said: "Each year's Summer Review precedents are applied in Beijing but not in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In 1506 Yang Shousui, Minister of Works and acting director of the Court of Judicial Review, noted that Summer Review precedents were enforced in Beijing but not Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 五年一審錄事例，行於在京，而略於在外。

translations.literal: The five-year joint review precedent is applied in the capital but slighted in the provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The five-year joint review was observed in the capital but neglected in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 今宜通行南京，凡審囚，三法司皆會審，其在外審錄，亦依此例。」

translations.literal: Now Nanjing should be included; whenever prisoners are tried, all three judicial offices should sit together, and provincial joint reviews should follow the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: He urged extending both practices to Nanjing and the provinces, with all three judicial offices sitting together at every review.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十年，令每年熱審並五年審錄之期，雜犯死罪、準徒五年者，皆減一年。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiajing, it was ordered that in each year's Summer Review and in the five-year joint review period, for miscellaneous capital offenses and those commutable to five years' penal servitude, one year was to be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: In 1531 an order required that at each Summer Review and five-year joint review, miscellaneous capital offenses and those commutable to five years' penal servitude receive a one-year reduction.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，刑科羅崇奎言：「五、六月間，笞罪應釋放、徒罪應減等者，亦宜如成化時欽恤枷號例，暫與蠲免，至六月終止。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, remonstrance official Luo Chongkui of the punishment section said: "Between the fifth and sixth months, those liable to bamboo who should be released and those in penal servitude who should receive reduced sentences should, as under Chenghua's imperial commutation and cangue precedent, be temporarily exempted until the end of the sixth month.
translations.idiomatic: In 1544 Luo Chongkui of the punishment remonstrance section proposed that in the fifth and sixth months, prisoners due for release or reduction under Summer Review, following Chenghua's precedent, be temporarily exempted until the end of June.

sentences.zh: 南法司亦如之。」

translations.literal: The southern judicial offices should do likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The southern judicial offices should follow suit.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: Approval was returned.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 隆慶五年，令贓銀止十兩以上、監久產絕、或身故者，熱審免追，釋其家屬。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Longqing, it was ordered that for embezzled silver of only ten taels or more, where long imprisonment had exhausted the prisoner's property or the prisoner had died, collection was waived at Summer Review and the family released.
translations.idiomatic: In 1571 an order waived collection at Summer Review of embezzled silver of ten taels or more when long imprisonment had exhausted the prisoner's estate or the prisoner had died, and released the family.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三十九年，方大暑省刑，而熱審矜疑疏未下。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year of Wanli, amid great heat the emperor lightened punishments, yet the Summer Review commutation list had not been issued.
translations.idiomatic: In 1611, during an unusually hot summer when punishments were being lightened, the Summer Review commutation list had still not been issued.

sentences.zh: 刑部侍郎沈應文以獄囚久滯，乞暫豁矜疑者。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Punishment Shen Yingwen, because prisoners had long been detained, begged temporary application of the commutation for doubtful cases.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Shen Yingwen, citing long detention, begged temporary application of commutation for doubtful cases.

sentences.zh: 未報。

translations.literal: No reply was received.
translations.idiomatic: No answer came.

sentences.zh: 明日，法司盡按囚籍軍徒杖罪未結者五十三人，發大興、宛平二縣監候，乃以疏聞。

translations.literal: The next day the judicial offices, proceeding through the register of all prisoners in military exile, penal servitude, and bamboo punishments still unresolved, sent fifty-three persons to be held in custody in Daxing and Wanping counties, and then reported by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the judicial offices went through their registers and sent fifty-three prisoners still in military exile, penal servitude, or bamboo sentences to custody in Daxing and Wanping counties before memorializing the throne.

sentences.zh: 神宗亦不罪也。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong also did not punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong did not punish them either.

sentences.zh: 舊例，每年熱審自小滿後十餘日，司禮監傳旨下刑部，即會同都察院、錦衣衛題請，通行南京法司，一體審擬具奏。

translations.literal: By the old rule, each year's Summer Review, starting some ten days after Lesser Fullness, the Directorate of Ceremonial transmitted an edict to the Ministry of Punishment, which then jointly with the Censorate and Embroidered-Uniform Guard memorialized and ordered the Nanjing judicial offices to deliberate uniformly and memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rule, Summer Review began about ten days after Lesser Fullness, when the Directorate of Ceremonial transmitted an edict to the Ministry of Punishment, which with the Censorate and Embroidered-Uniform Guard ordered the Nanjing courts to deliberate and report jointly.

sentences.zh: 京師自命下之日至六月終止。

translations.literal: In the capital, from the day the order was issued until the end of the sixth month.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital the period ran from the day the order was issued to the end of the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 南京自部移至日為始，亦滿兩月而止。

translations.literal: At Nanjing it began when the ministry received the document and likewise lasted two months.
translations.idiomatic: At Nanjing it began when the ministry received the document and likewise lasted two months.

sentences.zh: 四十四年不舉行。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year it was not held.
translations.idiomatic: In 1616 it was not held.

sentences.zh: 明年，又逾兩月，命未下，會暑雨，獄中多疫。

translations.literal: The next year, again more than two months passed without an order; amid summer rains, plague spread in the prisons.
translations.idiomatic: The following year more than two months passed without an order; amid summer rains plague spread through the prisons.

sentences.zh: 言官以熱審愆期、朝審不行、詔獄理刑無人三事交章上請。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials submitted successive memorials on three matters: the delayed Summer Review, the failure to hold the Court Review, and the absence of anyone to judge cases in the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Censors memorialized in succession on three points: the delayed Summer Review, the omitted Court Review, and the lack of judges for the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 又請釋楚宗英嫶、蘊鈁等五十餘人，罣誤知縣滿朝薦，同知王邦才、卞孔時等。

translations.literal: They also requested release of more than fifty persons including Ying Miao and Yun Qian of the Chu princely house, and the wrongly implicated magistrate Man Chaojian and vice magistrates Wang Bangcai and Bian Kongshi.
translations.idiomatic: They also asked release of more than fifty people, including Ying Miao and Yun Qian of the Chu princely line, the wrongly implicated magistrate Man Chaojian, and vice magistrates Wang Bangcai and Bian Kongshi.

sentences.zh: 皆不報。

translations.literal: None received reply.
translations.idiomatic: None received answer.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十五年四月亢旱，下詔清獄。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifteenth year of Chongzhen, amid severe drought, an edict ordered prisons cleared.
translations.idiomatic: In April 1642, during severe drought, an edict ordered the prisons cleared.

sentences.zh: 中允黃道周言：「中外齋宿為百姓請命，而五日之內系兩尚書，不聞有抗疏爭者，尚足迴天意乎？」

translations.literal: Palace lecturer Huang Daozhou said: "Inside and outside the court, fasting and purification are observed to plead for the people's lives, yet within five days two ministers are imprisoned, and I hear no one submitting a bold memorial of protest—can this turn back Heaven's mind?
translations.idiomatic: Palace lecturer Huang Daozhou protested: "Court and country observe fasting to plead for the people, yet within five days two ministers are imprisoned and no one dares remonstrate boldly—how can this move Heaven?

sentences.zh: 兩尚書謂李日宣、陳新甲也。

translations.literal: The two ministers were Li Rixuan and Chen Xinji.
translations.idiomatic: The two ministers were Li Rixuan and Chen Xinji.

sentences.zh: 帝方重怒二人，不能從。

translations.literal: The emperor was then deeply angry with the two men and could not comply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then too angry with the two men to comply.

sentences.zh: 歷朝無寒審之制，崇禎十年，以代州知州郭正中疏及寒審，命所司求故事。

translations.literal: No dynasty had a Winter Review system; in the tenth year of Chongzhen, because of a memorial from Guo Zhengzhong, magistrate of Daizhou, on Winter Review, offices were ordered to seek precedents.
translations.idiomatic: No dynasty had maintained a Winter Review; in 1637, after Daizhou magistrate Guo Zhengzhong memorialized on the subject, offices were ordered to search for precedents.

sentences.zh: 尚書鄭三俊乃引數事以奏，言：「謹按洪武二十三年十二月癸未，太祖諭刑部尚書楊靖，『自今惟犯十惡並殺人者論死，餘死罪皆令輸粟北邊以自贖』。

translations.literal: Minister Zheng Sanjun cited several matters and memorialized, saying: "According to the twelfth month, day guiwei, of the twenty-third year of Hongwu, the Founder instructed Minister of Punishment Yang Jing: 'From now on only those guilty of the ten abominations and murder shall be sentenced to death; for all other death sentences, order grain delivered to the northern frontier in redemption.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zheng Sanjun cited several precedents, including Hongwu 23 (1390), when Taizu told Minister Yang Jing: "Henceforth only the ten abominations and murder shall be punished by death; all other capital crimes may redeem themselves by delivering grain to the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 永樂四年十一月，法司進月繫囚數，凡數百人，大辟僅十之一。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Yongle, the judicial offices reported the month's prisoners in custody, several hundred in all; capital offenses were barely one in ten.
translations.idiomatic: In November 1406 the judicial offices reported several hundred prisoners in custody for the month; barely one in ten faced capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 成祖諭呂震曰：『此等既非死罪，而久系不決，天氣冱寒，必有聽其冤死者。』

translations.literal: Emperor Chengzu instructed Lü Zhen: "These are not death crimes, yet long detained without decision—in such bitter cold there must be some who die in prison though wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Chengzu told Lü Zhen: "These are not capital crimes, yet they linger unresolved—in such bitter cold some innocent must die in prison.

sentences.zh: 凡雜犯死罪下約二百，悉準贖發遣。

translations.literal: All miscellaneous capital offenses, about two hundred in all, were commuted by ransom and dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Some two hundred prisoners facing miscellaneous capital offenses were all commuted by ransom and released.

sentences.zh: 九年十一月，刑科曹潤等言：『昔以天寒，審釋輕囚。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the ninth year, remonstrance officials of the punishment section Cao Run and others said: "Formerly, because of cold weather, light prisoners were reviewed and released.
translations.idiomatic: In November 1411, Cao Run and others of the punishment remonstrance section said: "In former times, when the weather turned cold, light prisoners were reviewed and released."

sentences.zh: 今囚或淹一年以上，且一月間瘐死者九百三十餘人，獄吏之毒所不忍言。』

translations.literal: Now prisoners are sometimes detained more than a year, and in a single month more than nine hundred thirty died of illness in prison—the cruelty of jailers is more than one can bear to tell.
translations.idiomatic: Today some prisoners languish more than a year, and in one month alone over nine hundred thirty died of sickness in custody—what the jailers do is beyond words.

sentences.zh: 成祖召法司切責，遂詔：『徒流以下三日內決放，重罪當系者恤之，無令死於饑寒。』

translations.literal: Emperor Chengzu summoned the judicial offices and sternly rebuked them, then issued an edict: "For penal servitude and exile and below, decide and release within three days; for heavy crimes that must be detained, show compassion, and do not let them die of hunger and cold."
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu summoned the judicial offices, rebuked them sharply, and ordered: "Release all penal servitude and exile cases within three days; for serious offenses that must be held, show mercy—do not let them die of hunger or cold."

sentences.zh: 十二年十一月，復令以疑獄名上，親閱之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the twelfth year, it was again ordered that doubtful cases be reported by name for personal review.
translations.idiomatic: In November 1414 he again ordered doubtful cases reported by name for his personal review.

sentences.zh: 宣德四年十月，以皇太子千秋節，減雜犯死罪以下，宥笞杖及枷鐐者。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Xuande, on the crown prince's birthday, miscellaneous capital offenses and below were reduced, and those liable to bamboo beating or wearing cangue and fetters were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In October 1429, on the crown prince's birthday, miscellaneous capital offenses and below were commuted, and those due for bamboo punishment or wearing cangue and fetters were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 嗣後，世宗、神宗或以災異修刑，或以覃恩佈德。

translations.literal: Thereafter Emperor Shizong and Emperor Shenzong sometimes lightened punishments because of omens, sometimes showed grace through general amnesties.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperors Shizong and Shenzong sometimes eased punishments after portents, sometimes granted mercy through general amnesties.

sentences.zh: 寒審雖無近例，而先朝寬大，皆所宜取法者。」

translations.literal: Although Winter Review had no recent precedent, the magnanimity of former reigns was all worthy of emulation.'
translations.idiomatic: Though Winter Review lacks recent precedent, the leniency of earlier reigns is worth following."

sentences.zh: 奏上，帝納其言。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor accepted his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 然永樂十一年十月，遣副都御史李慶齎璽書，命皇太子錄南京囚，贖雜犯死罪以下。

translations.literal: Yet in the tenth month of the eleventh year of Yongle, Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Qing was dispatched bearing imperial credentials ordering the crown prince to review Nanjing prisoners and ransom miscellaneous capital offenses and below.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in October 1413 Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Qing was sent with imperial credentials ordering the crown prince to review Nanjing prisoners and commute miscellaneous capital offenses and below.

sentences.zh: 宣德四年冬，以天氣冱寒，敕南北刑官悉錄繫囚以聞，不分輕重。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year of Xuande, because the weather was bitterly cold, an edict ordered northern and southern penal officials all to record prisoners in custody and report, without distinction of severity.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of 1429, because the weather was bitterly cold, an edict ordered penal officials north and south to report all prisoners in custody, regardless of severity.

sentences.zh: 因謂夏原吉等曰：「堯、舜之世，民不犯法，成、康之時，刑措不用，皆君臣同德所致。

translations.literal: He then said to Xia Yuanji and others: "In the age of Yao and Shun the people did not break the law; in the time of Cheng and Kang punishments were set aside unused—all arose from ruler and ministers sharing the same virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He told Xia Yuanji and others: "Under Yao and Shun the people did not offend; under Cheng and Kang punishments fell unused—all because ruler and ministers shared one virtue.

sentences.zh: 朕德薄，卿等其勉力匡扶，庶無愧古人。」

translations.literal: My virtue is slight; you must strive to support me, that we may not fall short of the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: My virtue is slight. Strive to support me, that we may not shame the ancients.

sentences.zh: 此寒審最著者，三俊亦不暇詳也。

translations.literal: This was the most notable Winter Review; Sanjun also had no leisure to elaborate.
translations.idiomatic: This was the most famous Winter Review; Sanjun did not elaborate further.

sentences.zh: 在外恤刑會審之例，定於成化時。

translations.literal: The precedent for joint compassionate review of cases in the provinces was fixed in the Chenghua period.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial compassionate joint review was established in the Chenghua reign.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖患刑獄壅蔽，分遣御史林願、石恆等治各道囚，而敕諭之。

translations.literal: Initially the Founder, troubled by obstruction in penal cases, dispatched censors Lin Yuan, Shi Heng, and others to handle prisoners in each circuit, and admonished them.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Taizu, troubled by blocked justice, sent censors Lin Yuan, Shi Heng, and others to handle prisoners in each circuit with stern instructions.

sentences.zh: 宣宗夜讀《周官·立政》：「式敬爾由獄，以長我王國。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong read at night in the "Establishment of Government" chapter of the Zhou Offices: "Reverently handle your prisons, to extend my royal domain.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong read at night in the Zhou Offices: "Reverently conduct your prisons, to extend my royal domain.

sentences.zh: 慨然興歎，以為立國基命在於此。

translations.literal: He sighed deeply, thinking that establishing the foundation of the state lay in this.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed, believing the foundation of the state lay in this.

sentences.zh: 乃敕三法司：「朕體上帝好生之心，惟刑是恤。

translations.literal: He then instructed the Three Judicial Offices: "I embody the Lord on High's mind of cherishing life and am concerned only with punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He instructed the Three Judicial Offices: "I embody Heaven's love of life and am concerned above all with punishments.

sentences.zh: 令爾等詳覆天下重獄，而犯者遠在千萬里外，需次當決，豈能無冤？」

translations.literal: Now I order you to review in detail heavy cases throughout the realm, yet offenders are far away thousands of li, awaiting their turn for execution—how can there be no wrongful convictions?
translations.idiomatic: I order you to review capital cases throughout the realm, yet prisoners thousands of li away, awaiting execution—how can there be no injustice?

sentences.zh: 因遣官審錄之。

translations.literal: Officials were therefore dispatched to review records.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were dispatched to review records.

sentences.zh: 正統六年四月，以災異頻見，敕遣三法司官詳審天下疑獄。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixth year of Zhengtong, because omens appeared frequently, an edict dispatched Three Judicial Office officials to review in detail doubtful cases throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In April 1441, because omens recurred, an edict sent Three Judicial Office officials to review doubtful cases empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 於是御史張驥、刑部郎林厚、大理寺正李從智等十三人同奉敕往，而復以刑部侍郎何文淵、大理卿王文、巡撫侍郎周忱、刑科給事中郭瑾審兩京刑獄，亦賜敕。

translations.literal: Thereupon censor Zhang Ji, Ministry of Punishment registrar Lin Hou, Court of Judicial Review director Li Congzhi, and thirteen others together received the edict and departed; Vice Minister of Punishment He Wenyuan, Court of Judicial Review director Wang Wen, grand coordinator Vice Minister Zhou Chen, and remonstrance official Guo Jin were also appointed to review penal cases in the two capitals, likewise receiving credentials.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Ji, registrar Lin Hou, director Li Congzhi, and thirteen others went forth; Vice Minister He Wenyuan, director Wang Wen, grand coordinator Zhou Chen, and remonstrance official Guo Jin reviewed the two capitals, all bearing imperial credentials.

sentences.zh: 後評事馬豫言：「臣奉敕審刑，竊見各處捉獲強盜，多因仇人指攀，拷掠成獄，不待詳報，死傷者甚多。

translations.literal: Later evaluating official Ma Yu said: "Your servant received the edict to review punishments and observed that bandits captured everywhere were often implicated by enemies; under torture cases were made up, and without awaiting detailed report many died or were injured.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ma Yu reported: "Reviewing punishments, I found captured bandits often accused by enemies; under torture false confessions were extracted, and many died before proper report.

sentences.zh: 今後宜勿聽妄指，果有贓證，御史、按察司會審，方許論決。

translations.literal: Henceforth rash accusations should not be heard; only when there is genuine evidence of booty should censors and surveillance commissioners jointly review before sentence is passed.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth rash accusations should not be accepted; only with real evidence should censors and surveillance commissioners jointly try before sentencing.

sentences.zh: 若未審錄有傷死者，毋得準例升賞。」

translations.literal: If before review there are deaths or injuries, promotion and reward should not be granted according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: If prisoners die or are injured before review, no promotion or reward should follow precedent.

sentences.zh: 是年，出死囚以下無數。

translations.literal: That year, death-row prisoners and below without number were released.
translations.idiomatic: That year countless death-row prisoners and below were released.

sentences.zh: 九年，山東副使王裕言：「囚獄當會審，而御史及三司官或逾年一會，囚多瘐死。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Shandong vice commissioner Wang Yu said: "Prisoners should be jointly reviewed, yet censors and officials of the three offices sometimes meet only once a year, and many prisoners die of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1444 Shandong vice commissioner Wang Yu said: "Prisoners should be jointly reviewed, yet censors and the three offices sometimes meet only once a year, and many die in custody.

sentences.zh: 往者常遣御史會按察司詳審，釋遣甚眾。

translations.literal: Formerly censors were often dispatched to join surveillance commissioners in detailed review, and very many were released.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly dispatched censors joined surveillance commissioners in detailed review and released very many.

sentences.zh: 今莫若罷會審之例，而行詳審之法，敕遣按察司官一員，專審諸獄。」

translations.literal: Now it would be better to abolish joint review and carry out detailed review: order one surveillance commissioner specially to review all prisons.
translations.idiomatic: Better to abolish joint review and appoint one surveillance commissioner solely to review all prisons.

sentences.zh: 部持舊制不可廢。

translations.literal: The ministry held that the old system could not be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry held the old system could not be abolished.

sentences.zh: 帝命審例仍舊，復如詳審例，選按察司官一員與巡按御史同審。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that the review precedent remain as before, but also as in the detailed review precedent, selecting one surveillance commissioner to review together with the touring censor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kept joint review but also, as in detailed review, ordered one surveillance commissioner to sit with the touring censor.

sentences.zh: 失出者姑勿問，涉贓私者究如律。

translations.literal: Those who wrongly released prisoners were for the time not questioned; those involved in embezzlement were prosecuted according to the code.
translations.idiomatic: Those who wrongly released prisoners were not punished for the time; embezzlers were prosecuted under the code.

sentences.zh: 成化元年，南京戶部侍郎陳翼因災異復請如正統例。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chenghua, Nanjing Vice Minister of Revenue Chen Yi, because of omens, again requested following the Zhengtong precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1465 Nanjing Vice Minister Chen Yi, citing omens, again asked to follow the Zhengtong precedent.

sentences.zh: 部議以諸方多事，不行。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated that because many regions were troubled, it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry declined because many regions were troubled.

sentences.zh: 八年，乃分遣刑部郎中劉秩等十四人會巡按御史及三司官審錄，敕書鄭重遣之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, fourteen persons including Ministry of Punishment registrar Liu Zhi were dispatched to join touring censors and officials of the three offices in joint review; credentials were solemnly bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1472 fourteen officials including registrar Liu Zhi were sent to join touring censors and the three offices, with solemn credentials.

sentences.zh: 十二年，大學士商輅言：「自八年遣官後，五年於茲，乞更如例行。」

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Grand Secretary Shang Lu said: "Since officials were dispatched in the eighth year, five years have passed; I beg that it again be done according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1476 Grand Secretary Shang Lu said: "Five years have passed since the eighth year; I beg it be done again as before.

sentences.zh: 帝從其請。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 至十七年，定在京五年大審。

translations.literal: By the seventeenth year, the five-year Grand Review in the capital was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1481 the capital's five-year Grand Review was fixed.

sentences.zh: 即於是年遣部寺官分行天下，會同巡按御史行事。

translations.literal: In that same year ministry and court officials were dispatched throughout the realm to join touring censors in action.
translations.idiomatic: That year ministry and court officials were sent throughout the realm to join touring censors.

sentences.zh: 於是恤刑者至，則多所放遣。

translations.literal: When compassionate reviewers arrived, very many were released.
translations.idiomatic: When compassionate reviewers arrived, very many were released.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十三年，定坐贓不及百兩，產絕者免監追。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year of Jiajing, it was fixed that for embezzlement of less than one hundred taels, when property was exhausted, prison surveillance was waived.
translations.idiomatic: In 1564 embezzlement under one hundred taels with exhausted property was exempted from continued detention for collection.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四年，敕雜犯死罪準徒五年者，並兩犯徒律應總徒四年者，各減一年，其他徒流等罪俱減等。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wanli, an edict ordered that miscellaneous capital offenses commutable to five years' penal servitude, and those under the statute of accumulated penal servitude of four years for two offenses, each received one year's reduction; other penal servitude, exile, and the like were all reduced one grade.
translations.idiomatic: In 1576 miscellaneous capital offenses commutable to five years' penal servitude and two-time penal servitude totaling four years each received one year's reduction; other penal servitude and exile were reduced one grade.

sentences.zh: 皆由恤刑者奏定。

translations.literal: All were fixed by memorial from compassionate reviewers.
translations.idiomatic: All were fixed by memorial from compassionate reviewers.

sentences.zh: 所生全者益多矣。

translations.literal: Those whose lives were spared grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Ever more lives were spared.

sentences.zh: 初，正統十一年，遣刑部郎中郭恂、員外郎陸瑜審南、北直隸獄囚，文職五品以下有罪，許執問。

translations.literal: Initially in the eleventh year of Zhengtong, Ministry of Punishment registrar Guo Xun and registrar Lu Yu were dispatched to review prisoners in the northern and southern directly administered areas; civil officials of the fifth rank and below who were guilty were permitted to be interrogated.
translations.idiomatic: In 1446 registrars Guo Xun and Lu Yu reviewed prisoners in the metropolitan districts; guilty civil officials of the fifth rank and below could be interrogated.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖間制，審錄官一省事竣，總計前後所奏，依準改駁多寡，通行考覈。

translations.literal: Under the Jiajing system, when a reviewing official finished one province, he totaled all memorials before and after, and according to the number of revisions and rejections, a general assessment was conducted.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiajing rules, when a reviewer finished a province, he totaled memorials and assessed according to revisions and rejections.

sentences.zh: 改駁數多者聽劾。

translations.literal: Those with many revisions and rejections were subject to impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Many revisions and rejections invited impeachment.

sentences.zh: 故恤刑之權重，而責亦匪輕。

translations.literal: Therefore the power of compassionate review was weighty, and the responsibility was not light.
translations.idiomatic: Compassionate review carried great power and no light responsibility.

sentences.zh: 此中外法司審錄之大較也。

translations.literal: This is the general outline of joint review by judicial offices inside and outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the general outline of joint review inside and outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 凡刑部問發罪囚，所司通將所問囚數，不問罪名輕重，分南北人各若干，送山東司，呈堂奏聞，謂之歲報。

translations.literal: For all prisoners whose cases the Ministry of Punishment had sent for judgment, the office concerned reported the number interrogated, without regard to severity of offense, apportioned southerners and northerners in fixed numbers, sent them to the Shandong Bureau, and presented to the hall for memorial—this was called the annual report.
translations.idiomatic: For prisoners the ministry had sent for judgment, the office reported numbers interrogated regardless of offense, apportioned southerners and northerners in fixed quotas to the Shandong Bureau, and memorialized—the annual report.

sentences.zh: 每月以見監罪囚奏聞，謂之月報。

translations.literal: Each month prisoners in custody were memorialized—this was called the monthly report.
translations.idiomatic: Each month prisoners in custody were reported—the monthly report.

sentences.zh: 其做工、運炭等項，每五日開送工科，填寫精微冊，月終分六科輪報之。

translations.literal: For labor, charcoal transport, and the like, every ten days lists were sent to the Works Section and entered in the minute register; at month's end the Six Offices reported in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Labor, charcoal transport, and similar tasks were reported every ten days to the Works Section in the minute register; at month's end the Six Offices reported in turn.

sentences.zh: 凡法官治囚，皆有成法，提人勘事，必齎精微批文。

translations.literal: For all judges handling prisoners there were fixed rules: to take persons and investigate affairs one must carry the minute approval document.
translations.idiomatic: Judges handling prisoners followed fixed rules: taking persons or investigating required the minute approval document.

sentences.zh: 京外官五品以上有犯必奏聞請旨，不得擅勾問罪。

translations.literal: Metropolitan and provincial officials of the fifth rank and above who committed offenses had to be memorialized and await imperial order; they could not be privately summoned and questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the fifth rank and above in the capital or provinces who offended had to be memorialized; they could not be summoned and questioned without authority.

sentences.zh: 在八議者，實封以聞。

translations.literal: Those within the eight deliberations were sealed in real covers and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Those within the eight deliberations were reported in sealed memorials.

sentences.zh: 民間獄訟，非通政司轉達於部，刑部不得聽理。

translations.literal: Civil litigation from the people, unless transmitted through the Office of Transmission to the ministry, could not be heard by the Ministry of Punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Private lawsuits reached the Ministry of Punishment only through the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 誣告者反坐，越訴者笞，擊登聞鼓不實者杖。

translations.literal: False accusers were punished in reverse; those who bypassed regular channels were beaten with bamboo; those who struck the petition drum without cause were cudgeled.
translations.idiomatic: False accusers were punished in reverse; those who bypassed channels were bambooed; those who struck the petition drum without cause were cudgeled.

sentences.zh: 訐告問官，必核實乃逮問。

translations.literal: Accusations against officials were investigated for truth before arrest and questioning.
translations.idiomatic: Accusations against officials were verified before arrest.

sentences.zh: 至罪囚打斷起發有定期，刑具有定器，停刑有定月日，檢驗屍傷有定法，恤囚有定規，籍沒亦有定物，惟復仇者無明文。

translations.literal: There were fixed periods for breaking off and dispatching prisoners, fixed instruments of punishment, fixed months and days for suspending execution, fixed methods for examining corpses, fixed rules for compassionate treatment of prisoners, and fixed goods for confiscation—only revenge had no explicit text.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners had fixed dispatch dates, punishments fixed instruments, suspension fixed seasons, corpses fixed examination methods, prisoners fixed compassionate rules, confiscation fixed lists—only revenge lacked explicit statute.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年，刑部尚書何喬新言：「舊制提人，所在官司必驗精微批文，與符號相合，然後發遣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongzhi, Minister of Punishment He Qiaoxin said: "Under the old system, when taking persons, the local office had to verify the minute approval document against the tally before dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: In 1488 Minister He Qiaoxin said: "Under the old system, local offices verified minute approval documents against tallies before dispatch.

sentences.zh: 此祖宗杜漸防微深意也。

translations.literal: This was the profound intent of the founders in stopping evil at the first sign.
translations.idiomatic: This was the founders' intent to stop evil at the outset.

sentences.zh: 近者中外提人，止憑駕帖，既不用符，真偽莫辨，奸人矯命，何以拒之？

translations.literal: Recently, inside and outside, persons are taken only on imperial credentials, without tallies; truth and falsehood cannot be distinguished, and how can one reject those who forge commands?
translations.idiomatic: Now persons are taken on imperial credentials alone, without tallies—truth cannot be distinguished, and forged orders cannot be refused.

sentences.zh: 請給批文如故。」

translations.literal: He requested that approval documents again be issued as before.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that approval documents be issued again as before.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此祖宗舊例，不可廢。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This is the founders' old precedent and cannot be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "This is the founders' precedent and cannot be abolished."

sentences.zh: 命復行之。

translations.literal: An order was issued to restore the practice.
translations.idiomatic: An order restored the practice.

sentences.zh: 然旗校提人，率齎駕帖。

translations.literal: Yet banner guards taking persons generally carried only imperial credentials.
translations.idiomatic: Yet banner guards generally carried only imperial credentials.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年，錦衣衛千戶白壽等齎駕帖詣科，給事中劉濟謂當以御批原本送科，使知其事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing, Embroidered-Uniform Guard thousand-commander Bai Shou and others brought imperial credentials to the remonstrance office; supervising secretary Liu Ji said the original imperial draft should be sent to the office so they would know the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In 1522 Guard thousand-commander Bai Shou brought credentials to the remonstrance office; supervising secretary Liu Ji said the original imperial draft should be sent to the office.

sentences.zh: 兩人相爭並列，上命檢成、弘事例以聞。

translations.literal: The two disputed side by side; the emperor ordered precedents from the Chenghua and Hongzhi reigns reported.
translations.idiomatic: The two disputed; the emperor ordered Chenghua and Hongzhi precedents reported.

sentences.zh: 濟復言，自天順時例即如此。

translations.literal: Ji again said that from the Tianshun period the precedent had been thus.
translations.idiomatic: Ji said the Tianshun precedent had been thus.

sentences.zh: 帝入壽言，責濟以狀對，亦無以罪也。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted Shou's statement, ordered Ji to answer according to the facts, and also could not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sided with Shou, ordered Ji to answer on the facts, and could not punish him.

sentences.zh: 天啟時，魏忠賢用駕帖提周順昌諸人，竟激蘇州之變。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi period, Wei Zhongxian used imperial credentials to take Zhou Shunchang and others, ultimately provoking the Suzhou uprising.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi, Wei Zhongxian used credentials to take Zhou Shunchang and others, provoking the Suzhou uprising.

sentences.zh: 兩畿決囚，亦必驗精微批。

translations.literal: For deciding prisoners in the two metropolitan areas, minute approval documents also had to be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Deciding prisoners in the two metropolitan areas also required verifying minute approval documents.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十一年，恤刑主事戴楩、吳元璧、呂顒等行急失與內號相驗，比至，與原給外號不合，為巡按御史所糾，納贖還職。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Jiajing, compassionate-review registrars Dai Yan, Wu Yuanbi, and Lü Yi, traveling in haste, matched inner tallies with outer; when they arrived, they did not match the originally issued outer tally and were impeached by the touring censor, ransomed, and restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1542 compassionate-review registrars Dai Yan, Wu Yuanbi, and Lü Yi, traveling in haste, mismatched inner and outer tallies; the touring censor impeached them, they ransomed, and returned to office.

sentences.zh: 成化時，六品以下官有罪，巡按御史輒令府官提問。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua period, when officials of the sixth rank and below were guilty, touring censors often ordered prefectural officials to take and question them.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chenghua, when officials of the sixth rank and below offended, touring censors often ordered prefectural officials to interrogate them.

sentences.zh: 陝西巡撫項忠言：「祖制，京外五品以上官有犯奏聞，不得擅勾問。

translations.literal: Shaanxi grand coordinator Xiang Zhong said: "Under the ancestral system, metropolitan and provincial officials of the fifth rank and above who offended were memorialized and could not be privately summoned and questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi grand coordinator Xiang Zhong said: "Under ancestral rule, officials of the fifth rank and above who offended were memorialized and could not be privately summoned.

sentences.zh: 今巡按輒提問六品官，甚乖律意，當聞於朝，命御史、按察司提問為是。」

translations.literal: Now touring censors take and question officials of the sixth rank, greatly contrary to the intent of the code; it should be reported to the court, and censors and surveillance commissioners should be ordered to take and question.
translations.idiomatic: Touring censors now interrogate sixth-rank officials, contrary to the code; censors and surveillance commissioners should do so instead.

sentences.zh: 乃下部議，從之。

translations.literal: The matter was sent to the ministry for deliberation and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry deliberated and approved.

sentences.zh: 凡罪在八議者，實封奏聞請旨，惟十惡不用此例。

translations.literal: For offenses within the eight deliberations, sealed memorials were submitted and imperial order awaited; only the ten abominations did not use this precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Offenses within the eight deliberations required sealed memorials and imperial order; only the ten abominations were excepted.

sentences.zh: 所屬官為上司非理淩虐，亦聽實封徑奏。

translations.literal: Subordinate officials who suffered unreasonable oppression from superiors were also permitted to memorialize directly in sealed covers.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates unreasonably oppressed by superiors could also memorialize directly in sealed covers.

sentences.zh: 軍官犯罪，都督府請旨。

translations.literal: When military officers committed offenses, the chief military commission requested imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers who offended required imperial order through the chief military commission.

sentences.zh: 諸司事涉軍官及呈告軍官不法者，俱密以實封奏，無得擅勾問。

translations.literal: When any office's affairs involved military officers, or when military officers' misconduct was reported, all were memorialized in sealed covers in secret; none might be privately summoned and questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs involving military officers or reports of their misconduct were memorialized in secret sealed covers; none might be privately summoned.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，順天巡按御史鄭存仁檄府縣，凡法司有所追取，不得輒發。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing period, Shuntian touring censor Zheng Cunren ordered prefectures and counties that whenever the judicial offices sought persons, they should not release them.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing, Shuntian touring censor Zheng Cunren ordered prefectures and counties not to release persons sought by the judicial offices.

sentences.zh: 尚書鄭曉考故事，民間詞訟非自通政司轉達，不得聽。

translations.literal: Minister Zheng Xiao examined precedents: civil litigation from the people, unless transmitted from the Office of Transmission, could not be heard.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zheng Xiao found that private lawsuits could not be heard unless transmitted from the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 而諸司有應問罪人，必送刑部，各不相侵。

translations.literal: When any office had prisoners to question, they had to be sent to the Ministry of Punishment; each did not encroach on the other.
translations.idiomatic: Offices with prisoners to question had to send them to the Ministry of Punishment; jurisdictions did not overlap.

sentences.zh: 曉乃言：「刑部追取人，府縣不當卻。

translations.literal: Xiao then said: "When the Ministry of Punishment seeks persons, prefectures and counties should not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao said: "When the ministry seeks persons, prefectures and counties must not refuse.

sentences.zh: 存仁違制，宜罪。」

translations.literal: Cunren violated the system and should be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Cunren violated the system and should be punished.

sentences.zh: 存仁亦執自下而上之律，論曉欺罔。

translations.literal: Cunren also held to the law of proceeding from below upward and accused Xiao of deception.
translations.idiomatic: Cunren cited the law of proceeding from below upward and accused Xiao of deception.

sentences.zh: 乃命在外者屬有司，在京者屬刑部。

translations.literal: An order was then issued that outside the capital authority belonged to local offices, and in the capital to the Ministry of Punishment.
translations.idiomatic: An order assigned authority outside the capital to local offices and in the capital to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 然自曉去位，民間詞訟，五城御史輒受之，不復遵祖制矣。

translations.literal: Yet after Xiao left office, civil litigation from the people was again received by censors of the Five Wards, no longer following the ancestral system.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiao left office, the Five Wards censors again received private lawsuits, abandoning the ancestral rule.

sentences.zh: 洪武時，有告謀反者勘問不實，刑部言當抵罪。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu period, when someone reported a plot of rebellion and investigation proved it false, the Ministry of Punishment said he should be punished in reverse.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu, when a report of rebellion proved false, the ministry said the accuser should be punished in reverse.

sentences.zh: 帝以問秦裕伯。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Qin Yubo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Qin Yubo.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「元時若此者罪止杖一百，蓋以開來告之路也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "In Yuan times, for such cases the punishment was only one hundred blows of the cangue, thereby opening the road for future accusers.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Under the Yuan such cases drew only one hundred blows of the cangue, to keep the road of accusation open.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「奸徒不抵，善人被誣者多矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If villains are not punished in reverse, many good people are slandered.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "If villains are not punished in reverse, many good people are slandered.

sentences.zh: 自今告謀反不實者，抵罪。」

translations.literal: From now on, those who report rebellion falsely shall be punished in reverse.
translations.idiomatic: From now on false reports of rebellion shall be punished in reverse.

sentences.zh: 學正孫詢訐稅使孫必貴為胡黨，又訐元參政黎銘常自稱老豪傑，謗訕朝廷。

translations.literal: School instructor Sun Xun accused tax commissioner Sun Bigui of being a Hu party member, and also accused former Yuan administrator Li Mingchang of calling himself an old hero and slandering the court.
translations.idiomatic: School instructor Sun Xun accused tax commissioner Sun Bigui of Hu affiliation and former Yuan administrator Li Mingchang of calling himself an old hero and slandering the court.

sentences.zh: 帝以告訐非儒者所為，置不問。

translations.literal: The emperor, holding that tale-bearing was not what scholars should do, set the matter aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, holding tale-bearing unworthy of scholars, set the matter aside.

sentences.zh: 永樂間定制，誣三四人杖徒，五六人流三千里，十人以上者淩遲，家屬徙化外。

translations.literal: Under the Yongle system, false accusation of three or four persons drew bamboo or penal servitude; five or six persons drew exile three thousand li; ten or more drew lingering death, with families banished beyond civilization.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongle rules, false accusation of three or four persons drew bamboo or penal servitude; five or six drew exile three thousand li; ten or more drew lingering death with families banished beyond civilization.

sentences.zh: 洪武末年，小民多越訴京師，及按其事，往往不實，乃嚴越訴之禁。

translations.literal: At the end of Hongwu, common people often bypassed channels to sue in the capital; when cases were investigated they were often not substantiated, and the prohibition on bypassing channels was therefore made strict.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Hongwu, common people often sued in the capital; investigation often found cases unsubstantiated, and bypassing channels was strictly forbidden.

sentences.zh: 命老人理一鄉詞訟，會裏胥決之，事重者始白於官，然卒不能止，越訴者日多。

translations.literal: Elders were ordered to handle litigation in one township, deciding with village clerks; only serious matters were reported to officials—yet in the end it could not be stopped, and those bypassing channels grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Elders were ordered to handle township litigation with village clerks; only grave matters went to officials—yet bypassing could not be stopped.

sentences.zh: 乃用重法，戍之邊。

translations.literal: Heavy punishment was then applied, banishing offenders to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy punishment was applied, banishing offenders to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 宣德時，越訴得實者免罪，不實仍戍邊。

translations.literal: In the Xuande reign, those who petitioned beyond their authority and were found correct were exempted from punishment; if unsubstantiated, they were still sent to border service.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuande reign, petitioners who overstepped procedure but proved their case were pardoned; those whose claims failed were still sent to serve on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 景泰中，不問虛實，皆發口外充軍，後不以為例也。

translations.literal: In the Jingtai period, regardless of truth or falsehood, all were sent to military service beyond the passes; this was later not taken as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jingtai, every such petitioner was sent beyond the passes for military service, whether the claim was true or false—a practice later abandoned as precedent.

sentences.zh: 凡訐告原問官司者，成化間定議，核究得實，然後逮問。

translations.literal: For all cases of accusing the original adjudicating officials, a ruling was fixed in the Chenghua period: only after investigation confirmed the substance would arrest and interrogation follow.
translations.idiomatic: For petitions accusing the officials who had originally heard a case, Chenghua-era rules required that the accusation be verified before any arrest or interrogation.

sentences.zh: 弘治時，南京御史王良臣按指揮周愷等怙勢黜貨，愷等遂訐良臣。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi period, Nanjing censor Wang Liangchen, while on inspection, denounced Commanders Zhou Kai and others for relying on power to dismiss rivals and take bribes; Kai and others then accused Liangchen.
translations.idiomatic: During Hongzhi, the Nanjing censor Wang Liangchen investigated and charged the commanders Zhou Kai and others with abusing their power to oust rivals and extort bribes; they retaliated by accusing Wang.

sentences.zh: 詔下南京法司逮繫會鞫。

translations.literal: An edict was issued ordering the Nanjing judicial offices to arrest and hold them for joint trial.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial order sent the case to the Nanjing judicial offices to arrest all parties and try them together.

sentences.zh: 侍郎楊守隨言：「此與舊章不合。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Yang Shousui said: "This does not accord with the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Yang Shousui argued: "This conflicts with established procedure.

sentences.zh: 請自今以後，官吏軍民奏訴，牽緣別事，摭拾原問官者，立案不行。

translations.literal: I request that henceforth, when officials, soldiers, and civilians submit memorials or lawsuits that drag in other matters and gather accusations against the original adjudicating officials, no case shall be opened.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, when officials, soldiers, or commoners lodge petitions or suits that wander into unrelated matters and dredge up charges against the original magistrates, no case should be opened on that basis.

sentences.zh: 所奏事仍令問結，虛詐者擬罪，原問官枉斷者亦罪。」

translations.literal: The matter petitioned shall still be investigated and concluded; those who are fraudulent shall be sentenced; original adjudicating officials who wrongly decided cases shall also be punished."
translations.idiomatic: The underlying complaint should still be heard to judgment; false accusers should be punished, and original officials who had wrongly decided the case should be punished as well."

sentences.zh: 乃下其議於三法司。

translations.literal: The proposal was then sent to the Three Judicial Offices.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was referred to the Three Judicial Offices.

sentences.zh: 法司覆奏如所請，從之。

translations.literal: The judicial offices memorialized approval as requested, and it was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial offices reported back endorsing the request, and the throne approved.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十六年以前，刑部令主事廳會御史、五軍斷事司、大理寺、五城兵馬指揮使官，打斷罪囚。

translations.literal: Before the twenty-sixth year of Hongwu, the Ministry of Punishment ordered the clerical bureau directors to convene with censors, officials of the Five Armies Adjudication Office, the Court of Judicial Review, and the Five City military patrol commanders to carry out executions of condemned prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: Before Hongwu 26, the Ministry of Punishment required its bureau directors to meet with censors, the Five Armies Adjudication Office, the Court of Judicial Review, and the Five City patrol commanders to carry out executions.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，並差錦衣衛官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, officials of the Embroidered Uniform Guard were also assigned.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, Embroidered Uniform Guard officers were added to the roster.
