sentences.zh: 其後惟主事會御史，將笞杖罪於打斷廳決訖，附卷，奉旨者次日覆命。

translations.literal: Thereafter only bureau directors met with censors; punishments of beating with the light and heavy bamboo were decided in the Execution Hall, attached to the dossier, and where the emperor's approval was required, the return report was made the next day.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward only bureau directors met with censors. Light and heavy bamboo sentences were decided in the Execution Hall, filed with the case, and when imperial approval was needed, a report was submitted the next day.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，刑部尚書孫丕揚言：「折獄之不速，由文移牽制故耳。

translations.literal: In the Wanli period, Minister of Punishment Sun Piyang said: "The slowness of deciding cases stems from being held back by paper shuffling.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wanli era, Minister Sun Piyang said: "Cases drag on because paperwork ties everything up.

sentences.zh: 議斷既成，部、寺各立長單，刑部送審掛號，次日即送大理。

translations.literal: Once deliberation is complete, each of the Ministry and the Court shall maintain a long register; the Ministry shall send the case for review and registration, and on the next day send it to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Once a judgment is settled, the Ministry and the Court should each keep a master docket: the Ministry registers the case for review and forwards it to the Court of Judicial Review the following day.

sentences.zh: 大理審允，次日即還本部。

translations.literal: Once the Court approved the review, it shall return the case to the Ministry the next day.
translations.idiomatic: When the Court approves the review, it should return the file to the Ministry the next day.

sentences.zh: 參差者究處，庶事體可一。

translations.literal: Those who delayed shall be investigated and punished, so that the whole process may be unified.
translations.idiomatic: Delays should be investigated and punished, so the process stays uniform.

sentences.zh: 至於打斷相驗，令御史三、六、九日遵例會同，餘日止會寺官以速遣。

translations.literal: As for execution and verification, censors shall meet on the third, sixth, and ninth days according to precedent; on other days only Court officials need meet to expedite dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: For executions and verification, censors should meet on the third, sixth, and ninth days as usual; on other days the Court alone may meet to speed dispatch.

sentences.zh: 徒流以上，部、寺詳鞫，笞杖小罪，聽堂部處分。」

translations.literal: For penal servitude, exile, and above, the Ministry and Court shall conduct detailed interrogation; for minor offenses of bamboo beating, the Ministry's main hall may dispose of them."
translations.idiomatic: Penal servitude, exile, and heavier penalties require full review by the Ministry and Court; minor bamboo offenses may be handled in the Ministry's main hall."

sentences.zh: 命如議行。

translations.literal: He was ordered to implement the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the reforms carried out.

sentences.zh: 凡獄囚已審錄，應決斷者限三日，應起發者限十日，逾銀計日以笞。

translations.literal: For prisoners already examined and recorded, those due for execution were limited to three days; those due for dispatch were limited to ten days; exceeding the limit was punished by bamboo strokes counted by day.
translations.idiomatic: Once prisoners had been examined and recorded, execution had to follow within three days and transfer within ten; each day over the limit brought a counted bamboo penalty.

sentences.zh: 囚淹滯至死者罪徒，此舊例也。

translations.literal: The punishment of those whose detention led to death was penal servitude—this was the old rule.
translations.idiomatic: Officials whose delay caused a prisoner to die in custody were sentenced to penal servitude—an old rule.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖六年，給事中周曁郎言：「比者獄吏苛刻，犯無輕重，概加幽系，案無新故，動引歲時。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiajing, Supervising Secretary Zhou Ji and others said: "Lately prison clerks have been harsh; regardless of gravity, they generally add secret imprisonment; cases without new grounds are routinely held year-round.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 6, Supervising Secretary Zhou Ji and others reported: "Jailers have grown cruel. Without regard to severity, they secretly detain everyone; stale cases are kept open year after year.

sentences.zh: 意喻色授之間，論奏未成，囚骨已糜。

translations.literal: Between a wink and a nod, the memorial of judgment has not yet been completed, and the prisoner's bones are already worn away.
translations.idiomatic: With a nod here and a look there, the judgment has not yet been filed and the prisoner is already dead in the cell.

sentences.zh: 又況偏州下邑，督察不及，奸吏悍卒倚獄為市，或扼其飲食以困之，或徙之穢溷以苦之，備諸痛楚，十不一生。

translations.literal: Moreover in remote prefectures and lower counties, where supervision does not reach, corrupt clerks and fierce guards treat the prison as a market, sometimes cutting off food and drink to wear them down, sometimes moving them to filthy latrines to torment them; after every kind of suffering, not one in ten survives.
translations.idiomatic: In remote prefectures and county seats, where oversight never reaches, venal clerks and brutal guards turn the jail into a marketplace—starving prisoners, dumping them in filth, inflicting every torment until fewer than one in ten survives.

sentences.zh: 臣觀律令所載，凡逮繫囚犯，老疾必散收，輕重以類分，枷杻薦席必以時飭，涼漿暖匣必以時備，無家者給之衣服，有疾者予之醫藥，淹禁有科，疏決有詔。

translations.literal: Your servant observes that the statutes provide: all arrested prisoners, the old and sick must be separately detained, heavy and light by category; cangues, shackles, mats and bedding must be maintained in season; cool soup and warm boxes must be prepared in season; those without families are given clothing, the sick are given medicine; there are penalties for excessive detention and edicts for periodic release.
translations.idiomatic: The code itself requires separate custody for the old and infirm, sorting prisoners by severity, timely upkeep of shackles, mats, and bedding, cool drink and warm boxes in season, clothes for the destitute, medicine for the sick, penalties for excessive detention, and periodic releases by edict.

sentences.zh: 此祖宗良法美意，宜敕臣下同為奉行。

translations.literal: These are the good laws and fine intent of the ancestral founders; Your Majesty should order your ministers jointly to carry them out.
translations.idiomatic: These were the founders' good laws and humane intent. Your Majesty should command officials everywhere to enforce them.

sentences.zh: 凡逮繫日月並已竟、未竟、疾病、死亡者，各載文冊，申報長吏，較其結竟之遲速，病故之多寡，以為功罪而黜陟之。」

translations.literal: For all periods of detention, completed and incomplete, sickness, and death, each shall be recorded in a register and reported to the senior official; comparing speed of conclusion and numbers of sickness and death shall serve as merit or fault for promotion and demotion."
translations.idiomatic: Every period of custody—finished or unfinished cases, illness, and death—should be logged and reported to the chief magistrate; the speed of closure and the toll of sickness and death should govern promotion and dismissal."

sentences.zh: 帝深然其言，且命中外有用法深刻，致戕民命者，即斥為民，雖才守可觀，不得推薦。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply approved the proposal, and also ordered that throughout the realm officials who used the law severely and thereby took the lives of the people should be dismissed as commoners; even if their talent and integrity were notable, they could not be recommended.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor strongly agreed and ordered that any official, inside or outside the capital, whose harsh use of law cost lives be stripped of office and reduced to commoner status—however able he might otherwise be, he was not to be recommended again.

sentences.zh: 凡內外問刑官，惟死罪並竊盜重犯，始用拷訊，餘止鞭撲常刑。

translations.literal: For all judicial officials within and without, only capital crimes together with grave cases of theft were to use torture in interrogation; the rest were limited to flogging and ordinary punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Judicial officers everywhere might use torture only in capital cases and major theft; all other offenses were limited to routine flogging.

sentences.zh: 酷吏輒用挺棍、夾棍、腦箍、烙鐵及一封書、鼠彈箏、攔馬棍、燕兒飛，或灌鼻、釘指，用徑寸懶杆、不去棱節竹片，或鞭脊背、兩踝致傷以上者，俱奏請，罪至充軍。

translations.literal: If cruel officials rashly used iron clubs, leg-presses, head-rings, branding irons, and the "sealed letter," "suspended zither," "blocking horse stick," "swallow in flight," or nose-pouring, nail-driving, inch-thick lazy poles, bamboo strips with nodes unremoved, or flogging the back and both ankles causing injury above the permitted level—all were to be memorialized and the offense reached military exile.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who used iron clubs, leg-presses, head-rings, branding irons, the sealed letter, mouse-harp, blocking-horse stick, swallow-in-flight, nose-pouring, nail-driving, unsmoothed bamboo rods, or flogging that broke back or ankles had to report upward; the penalty could reach military exile.

sentences.zh: 停刑之月，自立春以後，至春分以前。

translations.literal: The months of suspended punishment ran from after Establishing Spring until before the Spring Equinox.
translations.idiomatic: Executions were suspended from after Establishing Spring until the Spring Equinox.

sentences.zh: 停刑之日，初一、初八、十四、十五、十八、二十三、二十四、二十八、二十九、三十，凡十日。

translations.literal: The days of suspended punishment were the first, eighth, fourteenth, fifteenth, eighteenth, twenty-third, twenty-fourth, twenty-eighth, twenty-ninth, and thirtieth—ten days in all.
translations.idiomatic: Executions were also suspended on ten days each month: the 1st, 8th, 14th, 15th, 18th, 23rd, 24th, 28th, 29th, and 30th.

sentences.zh: 檢驗屍傷，照磨司取部印屍圖一幅，委五城兵馬司如法檢驗，府則通判、推官，州縣則長官親檢，毋得委下僚。

translations.literal: For examining corpse wounds, the Registry Office took an official corpse chart stamped with the ministry seal, and delegated the Five City military patrol office to examine according to law; in prefectures, the vice prefect and investigating magistrate; in departments and counties, the chief official personally examined—they must not delegate to subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: For forensic examination, the Registry Office issued an official corpse chart under the ministry seal and assigned the Five City patrol office to inspect by rule; in prefectures the vice prefect and investigating magistrate did so; in departments and counties the chief magistrate examined in person and could not delegate to subordinates.

sentences.zh: 獄囚貧不自給者，洪武十五年定制，人給米日一升。

translations.literal: For prisoners too poor to support themselves, regulations were set in the fifteenth year of Hongwu: each person received one sheng of rice per day.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners too poor to feed themselves were allotted one sheng of rice per day under Hongwu 15.

sentences.zh: 二十四年革去。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year this was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The allowance was abolished in the twenty-fourth year.

sentences.zh: 正統二年，以侍郎何文淵言，詔如舊，且令有贓罰敝衣得分給。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengtong, on the proposal of Vice Minister He Wenyuan, an edict restored the former practice, and ordered that confiscated clothing from fines for bribery might be distributed among them.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 2, on Vice Minister He Wenyuan's recommendation, the allowance was restored and worn-out clothes from bribery fines could be distributed to prisoners.

sentences.zh: 成化十二年，令有司買藥餌送部，又廣設惠民藥局，療治囚人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Chenghua, magistrates were ordered to buy medicines and send them to the ministry; Public Medicine Bureaus were also widely established to treat prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 12, local offices were ordered to buy medicines for the ministry, and Public Medicine Bureaus were expanded to treat prisoners.

sentences.zh: 至正德十四年，囚犯煤、油、藥料，皆設額銀定數。

translations.literal: By the fourteenth year of Zhengde, coal, oil, and medical supplies for prisoners were all set at fixed amounts of silver.
translations.idiomatic: By Zhengde 14, coal, lamp oil, and medical supplies for prisoners were funded by fixed silver quotas.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖六年，以運炭等有力罪囚，折色糴米，上本部倉，每年約五百石，乃停收。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiajing, prisoners convicted of strong offenses such as transporting coal were allowed to commute to rice tribute paid into the ministry granary, about five hundred shi per year, and then intake was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 6, able-bodied prisoners sentenced for offenses such as hauling coal could commute labor to rice paid into the ministry granary—about five hundred shi a year—after which general rice collection for prisoners was halted.

sentences.zh: 歲冬給綿衣褲各一事，提牢主事驗給之。

translations.literal: Each winter cotton jacket and trousers were issued one each; the duty officer of the prison verified and distributed them.
translations.idiomatic: Each winter every prisoner received one cotton jacket and one pair of trousers, issued by the prison duty officer after inspection.

sentences.zh: 犯罪籍沒者，洪武元年定制，自反叛外，其餘罪犯止沒田產孳畜。

translations.literal: For confiscation of property due to crime, regulations were set in the first year of Hongwu: apart from rebellion, other crimes confiscated only fields, property, and livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Property confiscation was first regulated in Hongwu 1: except for rebellion, other crimes forfeited only land, goods, and livestock.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，詔謀逆奸黨及造偽鈔者，沒貲產丁口，以農器耕牛給還之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, an edict provided that traitorous factions, conspirators, and forgers of paper money had assets and household members confiscated; farming tools and oxen were returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, an edict ordered confiscation of assets and household members for traitorous factions, conspiracy, and counterfeiting paper money, while farming tools and oxen were returned.

sentences.zh: 凡應合鈔劄者，曰奸黨，曰謀反大逆，曰奸黨惡，曰造偽鈔，曰殺一家三人，曰採生拆割人為首。

translations.literal: Those subject to paper warrants of confiscation included: traitorous factions; conspiracy and great treason; vicious traitorous factions; forging paper money; killing three members of one household; and leaders in kidnapping for organ harvesting.
translations.idiomatic: Cases requiring confiscation warrants included traitorous factions, conspiracy and great treason, vicious factions, counterfeiting paper money, killing three members of one household, and ringleaders in kidnapping for butchery.

sentences.zh: 其《大誥》所定十條，後未嘗用也。

translations.literal: The ten articles fixed in the Grand Pronouncements were later never applied.
translations.idiomatic: The ten articles laid down in the Grand Pronouncements were never used again.

sentences.zh: 復仇，惟祖父被毆條見之，曰：「祖父母、父母為人所殺，而子孫擅殺行兇人者，杖六十。

translations.literal: On revenge, only the article on grandparents being beaten appears, saying: "Where grandparents or parents were killed by others, and descendants on their own authority kill the perpetrator, they receive sixty blows of the light bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: On private revenge, only the clause on grandparents being assaulted survives: "If grandparents or parents were killed by another and a descendant kills the assailant on his own authority, he receives sixty blows of the light bamboo.

sentences.zh: 其即時殺死者勿論。

translations.literal: If they kill the person on the spot, no penalty applies.
translations.idiomatic: If he kills the assailant on the spot, no penalty applies.

sentences.zh: 其餘親屬人等被人殺而擅殺之者，杖一百。」

translations.literal: For other relatives and the like who were killed by others and are killed on one's own authority, one hundred blows of the light bamboo."
translations.idiomatic: For other relatives killed by another whom one kills on one's own authority, the penalty is one hundred blows of the light bamboo."

sentences.zh: 按律罪人應死，已就拘執，其捕者擅殺之，罪亦止此。

translations.literal: According to the code, where a criminal deserving death has already been taken into custody, if the captor kills him on his own authority, the penalty is likewise limited to this.
translations.idiomatic: By code, if a man deserving death is already in custody and his captor kills him without authority, the penalty is the same.

sentences.zh: 則所謂家屬人等，自包兄弟在內，其例可類推也。

translations.literal: Then the so-called household members and the like, brothers included within that term, may be inferred by analogy.
translations.idiomatic: The term "household members and the like" plainly includes brothers, and the rule may be extended by analogy.

sentences.zh: 凡決囚，每歲朝審畢，法司以死罪請旨，刑科三覆奏，得旨行刑。

translations.literal: For all executions of prisoners, each year after the Court Review was complete, the judicial offices requested imperial confirmation for death sentences; the Penal Affairs Section submitted three rehearing memorials, and upon receiving the directive, execution was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Each year, after the Court Review, the judicial offices sought imperial approval for death sentences; the Penal Affairs Section submitted three rehearing memorials, and execution followed the returned order.

sentences.zh: 在外者奏決單于冬至前，會審決之。

translations.literal: Those outside the capital submitted execution documents before the winter solstice, and after joint review the sentences were carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In the provinces, execution lists had to reach the throne before the winter solstice; after joint review, sentences were carried out.

sentences.zh: 正統元年，令重囚三覆奏畢，仍請駕帖，付錦衣衛監刑官，領校尉詣法司，取囚赴市。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong, after three rehearing memorials on grave prisoners were complete, an imperial credential was still requested and given to the supervising execution officer of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, who led guards to the judicial offices to take the prisoner to the execution ground.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 1, after three rehearings for capital convicts, an imperial credential was still required and given to the Embroidered Uniform Guard execution officer, who led guards to the judicial offices and escorted the prisoner to the execution ground.

sentences.zh: 又制，臨決囚有訴冤者，直登聞鼓給事中取狀封進，仍批校尉手，馳赴市曹，暫停刑。

translations.literal: Another rule provided: if at the moment of execution a prisoner pleaded injustice, he might directly strike the Drum of Direct Appeal; a supervising secretary of the appeal office took the petition, sealed it, and forwarded it; still marked in the guard's hand, he galloped to the execution ground and temporarily halted the execution.
translations.idiomatic: Another rule allowed a prisoner protesting innocence at execution to strike the Drum of Direct Appeal; a supervising secretary took the petition, sealed it, and a guard galloped to the execution ground to halt the sentence temporarily.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年，給事中劉濟等以囚廖鵬父子及王欽、陶傑等頗有內援，懼上意不決，乃言：「往歲三覆奏畢，待駕帖則已日午，鼓下仍受訴詞，得報且及未申時，及再請始刑，時已過酉，大非刑人於市與眾棄之之意。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing, Supervising Secretaries Liu Ji and others, because the prisoners Liao Peng, father and son, and Wang Qin, Tao Jie, and others had considerable inside support and feared the emperor's indecision, said: "In past years, after the three rehearings were complete, waiting for the imperial credential already reached noon; still accepting petitions below the drum, receiving response reached not yet the shen hour; only upon a second request was execution carried out, when it was already past you—greatly contrary to the intention of punishing men in the market before the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 1, Supervising Secretaries Liu Ji and others, fearing the emperor might hesitate over Liao Peng and his son, Wang Qin, Tao Jie, and others with powerful patrons, said: "After three rehearings, waiting for the imperial credential already brought noon; accepting drum petitions and awaiting reply stretched past mid-afternoon; a second request delayed execution until after the you hour—far from executing criminals publicly before the crowd as the law intends.

sentences.zh: 請自今決囚，在未前畢事。」

translations.literal: I request that henceforth executions of prisoners be completed before the wei hour."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth executions should be finished before the wei hour (1–3 p.m.)."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 七年定議，重囚有冤，家屬於臨決前一日撾鼓，翼日午前下，過午行刑，不覆奏。

translations.literal: In the seventh year a ruling was fixed: for grave prisoners with grievances, family members might beat the drum one day before execution; the next day before noon the petition was received; after noon execution was carried out without rehearing memorials.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year a rule was set: for capital prisoners claiming injustice, relatives could beat the drum the day before execution; if the petition arrived before noon the next day, execution waited; after noon it proceeded without rehearing.

sentences.zh: 南京決囚，無刑科覆奏例。

translations.literal: For executions in Nanjing, there was no precedent of rehearing memorials by the Penal Affairs Section.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing had no precedent of three rehearing memorials by the Penal Affairs Section.

sentences.zh: 弘治十八年，南刑部奏決不待時者三人，大理寺已審允，下法司議，謂：「在京重囚，間有決不待時者，審允奏請，至刑科三覆奏，或蒙恩仍監候會審。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Hongzhi, the Nanjing Ministry of Punishment reported three men for execution without waiting for the season; the Court of Judicial Review had approved review, and the case was sent to the judicial offices for deliberation, who said: "For grave prisoners in the capital, there are occasionally those executed without waiting for the season: after approval of review they memorialized and requested; upon three rehearings by the Penal Affairs Section, they might still receive mercy and be held for joint review.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 18, the Nanjing Ministry reported three men for immediate execution. The Court of Judicial Review had approved review, and the Three Judicial Offices deliberated: "In Beijing, some capital convicts are executed out of season after review approval and three Penal Affairs rehearings, and may still receive mercy and await joint review.

sentences.zh: 南京無覆奏例，乞俟秋後審竟，類奏定奪。

translations.literal: Nanjing has no precedent of rehearing memorials; I beg to wait until review is completed after autumn, then report in category for final decision.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing lacks rehearing precedent; we ask to wait until autumn review is complete and then report collectively for decision.

sentences.zh: 如有巨憝難依常例者，更具奏處決，著為令。」

translations.literal: If there are especially heinous cases hard to fit ordinary precedent, memorialize separately for execution and fix this as an order."
translations.idiomatic: For exceptionally heinous cases that cannot follow ordinary rules, report separately for execution and make this permanent law."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved.

sentences.zh: 各省決囚，永樂元年，定制，死囚百人以上者，差御史審決。

translations.literal: For executions in the provinces, in the first year of Yongle a rule was set: where death-row prisoners numbered one hundred or more, a censor was dispatched to review and decide.
translations.idiomatic: For provincial executions, Yongle 1 required a censor to review and decide when death sentences numbered one hundred or more.

sentences.zh: 弘治十三年，定歲差審決重囚官，俱以霜降後至，限期復命。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Hongzhi, officials annually dispatched to review and decide grave prisoners were fixed—all to arrive after the frost descent, with a deadline to report back.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 13, annual officers dispatched to review capital cases were fixed: all were to arrive after Frost Descent and report back by deadline.

sentences.zh: 凡有大慶及災荒皆赦，然有常赦，有不赦，有特赦。

translations.literal: For all great celebrations and disaster famines there were amnesties; yet there were regular amnesties, non-amnesties, and special amnesties.
translations.idiomatic: Great celebrations and disaster famines brought amnesties, but there were standing amnesties, exceptions, and special pardons.

sentences.zh: 十惡及故犯者不赦。

translations.literal: The ten abominations and intentional offenders were not amnestied.
translations.idiomatic: The ten abominations and deliberate offenders were not pardoned.

sentences.zh: 律文曰：「赦出臨時定罪名，特免或降減從輕者，不在此限。」

translations.literal: The statutes read: "Where amnesty is issued and the crime is fixed temporarily, specially exempted or reduced or mitigated—these are not within this limit."
translations.idiomatic: The code reads: "When amnesty is proclaimed and crimes are specified, those specially exempted or reduced are not within this limit."

sentences.zh: 十惡中，不睦又在會赦原宥之例，此則不赦者亦得原。

translations.literal: Among the ten abominations, lack of harmony toward relatives was also within cases restored on general amnesty; thus those not amnestied might also be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Among the ten abominations, "lack of harmony toward relatives" could still be restored under a general amnesty—so even unpardonable crimes might be remitted.

sentences.zh: 若傳旨肆赦，不別定罪名者，則仍依常赦不原之律。

translations.literal: If an imperial order proclaimed general amnesty without separately fixing the crimes, then the ordinary amnesty rule of non-restoration still applied.
translations.idiomatic: If an edict proclaimed amnesty without naming specific crimes, the ordinary rule against restoring unpardonable offenses still applied.

sentences.zh: 自仁宗立赦條三十五，皆楊士奇代草，盡除永樂年間敝政，歷代因之。

translations.literal: From the time Emperor Renzong established thirty-five amnesty provisions, all drafted by Yang Shiqi, abolishing abuses of the Yongle years; later dynasties followed this.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong set thirty-five amnesty articles—all drafted by Yang Shiqi—he swept away Yongle abuses, and later reigns followed suit.

sentences.zh: 凡先朝不便於民者，皆援遺詔或登極詔革除之。

translations.literal: For all matters of the previous reign inconvenient to the people, restoration was invoked through the testamentary edict or accession edict to abolish them.
translations.idiomatic: Harms to the people from the previous reign were commonly revoked in testamentary or accession edicts.

sentences.zh: 凡以赦前事告言人罪者，即坐以所告者罪。

translations.literal: For all who accused others of crimes on the basis of pre-amnesty matters, they were sentenced for the crime of which they accused others.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who denounced another for a pre-amnesty offense was punished with the crime he had alleged.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年，民呂梁山等四人坐竊盜殺人死，遇赦，都御史馬文升請宥死戍邊，帝特命依律斬之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongzhi, four men including Lu Liangshan were sentenced to death for theft and murder; meeting amnesty, Censor-in-Chief Ma Wensheng requested pardon and border service; the emperor specially ordered execution according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 1, Lu Liangshan and three others were condemned for robbery and murder. When amnesty came, Censor-in-Chief Ma Wensheng asked that they be spared for frontier service; the emperor ordered them executed according to law.

sentences.zh: 世宗雖屢停刑，尤慎無赦。

translations.literal: Though Emperor Shizong repeatedly suspended executions, he was especially cautious about granting amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Jiajing emperor often suspended executions, he was exceptionally reluctant to grant amnesty.

sentences.zh: 廷臣屢援赦令，欲宥大禮大獄暨建言諸臣，益持不允。

translations.literal: Court ministers repeatedly invoked amnesty orders, wishing to pardon those of the Great Rites and great prison cases and the memorializing officials; he held all the more firmly to refusal.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers repeatedly cited amnesty to free victims of the Great Rites controversy, major political trials, and memorializing officials; he refused all the more firmly.

sentences.zh: 及嘉靖十六年，同知薑輅酷殺平民，都御史王廷相奏當發口外，乃特命如詔書宥免，而以違詔責廷相等。

translations.literal: And in the sixteenth year of Jiajing, Assistant Prefect Jiang Yu cruelly killed commoners; Censor-in-Chief Wang Tingxiang memorialized that he should be sent beyond the passes; yet a special order pardoned him according to the proclamation, and Wang Tingxiang and others were rebuked for violating the proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 16, Assistant Prefect Jiang Yu brutally killed civilians. Censor-in-Chief Wang Tingxiang recommended exile beyond the passes, but a special edict pardoned Jiang under the amnesty proclamation and rebuked Wang for violating it.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，三殿成，羣臣請頒赦。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, the Three Hall complex was completed; the multitude of officials requested a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year, when the Three Hall complex was finished, officials petitioned for a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「赦乃小人之幸。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Amnesty is the fortune of petty men."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Amnesty is the luck of small men."

sentences.zh: 不允。

translations.literal: He did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 穆宗登極覃恩，雖徒流人犯已至配所者，皆許放還，蓋為遷謫諸臣地也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong acceded and extended universal grace, even convicts in penal servitude and exile who had already reached their place of assignment were all permitted to return—this was mainly to make room for the banished officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong took the throne and proclaimed universal grace, even convicts already at their places of assignment were allowed to return—chiefly to recall the banished officials.

sentences.zh: 有明一代刑法大概。

translations.literal: Such was the general outline of punitive law in the Ming dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Such, in broad outline, was Ming criminal law.

sentences.zh: 太祖開國之初，懲元季貪冒，重繩贓吏，揭諸司犯法者於申明亭以示戒。

translations.literal: At the founding of the realm, the Grand Ancestor, punishing the greed of the Yuan era, strictly bound corrupt officials and posted lawbreaking officials of each agency at the Declaration Pavilions as warning.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding, the Hongwu emperor, reacting to Yuan corruption, bound corrupt officials severely and posted the names of lawbreakers at Declaration Pavilions as warning.

sentences.zh: 又命刑部，凡官吏有犯，宥罪復職，書過榜其門，使自省。

translations.literal: He also ordered the Ministry of Punishment: whenever officials committed offenses, if pardoned and restored to office, their faults were written on placards at their gates for self-reflection.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the Ministry of Punishment that pardoned officials returning to office should have their offenses posted at their gates for self-examination.

sentences.zh: 不悛，論如律。

translations.literal: If they did not reform, they were sentenced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: If they did not reform, they were punished by law.

sentences.zh: 累頒犯諭、戒諭、榜諭，悉象以刑，誥示天下。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promulgating injunctions against violation, admonitions, and posted warnings—all illustrated with punishments, proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly issued violation injunctions, admonitions, and posted warnings—illustrated with punishments—and proclaimed them throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 及十八年《大誥》成，序之曰：「諸司敢不急公而務私者，必窮搜其原而罪之。」

translations.literal: When the Grand Pronouncements of the eighteenth year were completed, he prefaced them: "If any agency dares not serve the public but pursue private ends, the root shall be thoroughly traced and guilt imposed."
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Pronouncements were completed in the eighteenth year, he wrote in the preface: "Any office that neglects the public for private gain will have its root traced and be punished."

sentences.zh: 凡三《誥》所列淩遲、梟示、種誅者，無慮千百，棄市以下萬數。

translations.literal: All three Pronouncements listed dismemberment, exposure of the head, and extermination of clans numbering no less than hundreds; those below abandonment in the market numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: All three compilations prescribed dismemberment, exposure of the head, and extermination of clans by the hundreds; executions below abandonment in the market ran into the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 貴溪儒士夏伯啟叔侄斷指不仕，蘇州人才姚潤、王謨被徵不至，皆誅而籍其家。

translations.literal: The Guixi scholar Xia Boqi, uncle and nephew, cut off fingers and refused office; the Suzhou men of talent Yao Run and Wang Mo were summoned and did not come—all were executed and their households registered for confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: The Guixi scholar Xia Boqi and his nephew cut off their fingers rather than serve; the Suzhou talents Yao Run and Wang Mo ignored summons—all were executed and their property confiscated.

sentences.zh: 「寰中士夫不為君用。」

translations.literal: "Men of learning throughout the realm who do not serve the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: "Scholars throughout the realm who refuse to serve the ruler.

sentences.zh: 之科所由設也。

translations.literal: The statute was established from this.
translations.idiomatic: The statute against such refusal dates from these cases.

sentences.zh: 其《三編》稍寬容，然所記進士監生罪名，自一犯至四犯者猶三百六十四人。

translations.literal: Its Third Compilation was somewhat more lenient; yet jinshi and student offenses recorded ranged from one offense to four offenses, still three hundred sixty-four persons.
translations.idiomatic: The Third Compilation was somewhat milder, yet it still recorded 364 jinshi and students with one to four offenses each.

sentences.zh: 幸不死還職，率戴斬罪治事。

translations.literal: Those fortunate enough not to die and return to office mostly wore the suspended death sentence while conducting affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Those who survived and returned to office mostly served under suspended death sentences.

sentences.zh: 其推原中外貪墨所起，以六曹為罪魁，郭桓為誅首。

translations.literal: In tracing the origin of corruption within and without, the Six Ministries were taken as chief culprits, with Guo Huan as the head executed.
translations.idiomatic: Tracing corruption inside and outside government, the Six Ministries were treated as chief culprits, with Guo Huan as the principal victim.

sentences.zh: 郭桓者，戶部侍郎也。

translations.literal: Guo Huan was Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huan was Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 帝疑北平二司官吏李彧、趙全德等與桓為奸利，自六部左右侍郎下皆死，贓七百萬，詞連直省諸官吏，系死者數萬人。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected officials of the two commissions of Beiping, Li Yu, Zhao Quande, and others, of corrupt profit with Huan; from vice ministers left and right of the Six Ministries downward all were executed; illicit gains totaled seven million; accusations extended to officials of directly governed provinces; those implicated to death numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected Beiping commission officials Li Yu, Zhao Quande, and others of colluding with Huan for profit. From the Six Ministries' vice ministers downward, all were executed. Illicit gains totaled seven million; accusations spread to provincial officials, and tens of thousands died in the affair.

sentences.zh: 核贓所寄借遍天下，民中人之家大抵皆破。

translations.literal: The places where illicit goods were deposited and lent spread throughout the realm; middling households among the people were largely ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Deposits and loans tied to the case spread nationwide, ruining most middling households.

sentences.zh: 時鹹歸謗御史餘敏、丁廷舉。

translations.literal: At the time blame was widely cast on Censors Yu Min and Ding Tingju.
translations.idiomatic: At the time public blame fell heavily on Censors Yu Min and Ding Tingju.

sentences.zh: 或以為言，帝乃手詔列桓等罪，而論右審刑吳庸等極刑，以厭天下心，言：「朕詔有司除奸，顧復生奸擾吾民，今後有如此者，遇赦不宥。」

translations.literal: Some spoke of this; the emperor then personally drafted an edict listing the crimes of Huan and others, and sentenced Vice Director of the Right Court of Penal Review Wu Yong and others to extreme penalties to satisfy the hearts of all under Heaven, saying: "My edict ordered officials to eliminate traitors, yet again traitors arise to harass my people; henceforth whoever does so shall not be pardoned on amnesty."
translations.idiomatic: When this was raised, the emperor personally drafted an edict listing Huan's crimes and sentenced Vice Director Wu Yong of the Right Court of Penal Review and others to extreme penalties to satisfy public outrage, declaring: "I ordered corruption rooted out, yet traitors still harass my people; hereafter such offenders shall not be pardoned."

sentences.zh: 先是，十五年空印事發。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the fifteenth year the blank-seal affair broke out.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the fifteenth year, the blank-seal scandal erupted.

sentences.zh: 每歲布政司、府州縣吏詣戶部核錢糧、軍需諸事，以道遠，預持空印文書，遇部駁即改，以為常。

translations.literal: Each year officials of provincial administration commissions and prefectures, departments, and counties went to the Ministry of Revenue to verify grain taxes, military supplies, and other matters; because the road was long, they beforehand carried blank-seal documents, and when the ministry rejected them they altered them—this became routine.
translations.idiomatic: Each year provincial and local officials traveled to the Ministry of Revenue to reconcile grain taxes and military supplies. Because the journey was long, they routinely carried documents with blank seals and altered them whenever the ministry rejected an entry.

sentences.zh: 及是，帝疑有奸，大怒，論諸長吏死，佐貳榜百戍邊。

translations.literal: When this affair arose, the emperor suspected fraud, was greatly enraged, and sentenced the chief officials to death and their assistants and deputies to one hundred blows and border service.
translations.idiomatic: When the scandal broke, the emperor suspected fraud, flew into a rage, condemned the chief officials to death, and punished their deputies with a hundred blows and frontier exile.

sentences.zh: 甯海人鄭士利上書訟其冤，復杖戍之。

translations.literal: Zheng Shili of Ninghai submitted a memorial pleading their innocence and was again beaten and sent to border service.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Shili of Ninghai petitioned in their defense and was flogged and sent to the frontier again.

sentences.zh: 二獄所誅殺已過當。

translations.literal: The two cases executed and killed beyond what was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The two prosecutions killed far more people than the offenses warranted.

sentences.zh: 而胡惟庸、藍玉兩獄，株連死者且四萬。

translations.literal: In the Hu Weiyong and Lan Yu cases, those implicated to death numbered nearly forty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu Weiyong and Lan Yu purges implicated nearly forty thousand deaths.

sentences.zh: 然時引大體，有所縱舍。

translations.literal: Yet at the time he generally upheld the larger principle and sometimes showed leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, he usually kept the larger principle in view and sometimes showed mercy.

sentences.zh: 沅陵知縣張傑當輸作，自陳母賀，當元季亂離守節，今年老失養。

translations.literal: Zhang Jie, magistrate of Yuanling, was due for corvée labor and personally stated that his mother He, during the chaos of the Yuan end, had preserved her integrity; she was now old and lacked support.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jie, magistrate of Yuanling, was sentenced to corvée. He pleaded that his mother He had kept her integrity through the chaos at the end of the Yuan and was now old and unsupported.

sentences.zh: 帝謂可勵俗，特赦之，秩傑，令終養。

translations.literal: The emperor said this could encourage custom, specially pardoned him, restored his rank, and ordered him to care for his mother to the end.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said the case could encourage public virtue, pardoned Zhang, restored his rank, and ordered him to support his mother for life.

sentences.zh: 給事中彭與民坐系，其父為上表訴哀。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Peng Yumin was imprisoned; his father submitted a memorial to the throne pleading in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Peng Yumin was imprisoned; his father submitted a tearful petition to the throne.

sentences.zh: 立釋之，且免同系十七人。

translations.literal: He was immediately released, and seventeen others imprisoned with him were also pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Peng was released at once, and seventeen co-prisoners were pardoned with him.

sentences.zh: 有死囚妻妾訴夫冤，法司請黥之。

translations.literal: There were wives and concubines of death-row prisoners who pleaded their husbands' injustice; the judicial offices requested tattooing them.
translations.idiomatic: When wives of death-row prisoners petitioned that their husbands were innocent, the judicial offices asked to tattoo the women as false accusers.

sentences.zh: 帝以婦為夫訴，職也，不罪。

translations.literal: The emperor said that for a wife to plead for her husband was her duty, and they were not punished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said a wife pleading for her husband was only doing her duty, and they went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 都察院當囚死者二十四人，命羣臣鞫，有冤者，減數人死。

translations.literal: The Censorate reported twenty-four prisoners due for death; the emperor ordered the multitude of officials to interrogate them, and where there was injustice, several were removed from the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: When the Censorate reported twenty-four men for execution, the emperor ordered ministers to re-examine them and spared several who proved unjustly condemned.

sentences.zh: 真州民十八人謀不軌，戮之，而釋其母子當連坐者。

translations.literal: Eighteen men of Zhenzhou plotted rebellion and were executed, but the mother and son subject to collective punishment were released.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen men of Zhenzhou were executed for plotting rebellion, but a mother and son who would have been punished by association were released.

sentences.zh: 所用深文吏開濟、詹徽、陳甯、陶凱輩，後率以罪誅之。

translations.literal: The harsh legalists employed, such as Kai Ji, Zhan Hui, Chen Ning, and Tao Kai, were later mostly executed for crimes themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The harsh legalists he used—Kai Ji, Zhan Hui, Chen Ning, Tao Kai, and others—were themselves mostly executed for crimes later on.

sentences.zh: 亦數宣仁言，不欲純任刑罰。

translations.literal: He also often proclaimed benevolent words and did not wish to rely on punishment alone.
translations.idiomatic: He also often spoke in a benevolent tone and did not want to govern by punishment alone.

sentences.zh: 嘗行郊壇，皇太子從，指道旁荊楚曰：「古用此為撲刑，取能去風，雖寒不傷也。」

translations.literal: Once while proceeding to the suburban altar, the heir apparent followed; pointing to thorns and brambles by the road he said: "In antiquity these were used for flogging punishment, because they can dispel wind; though cold, they do not harm."
translations.idiomatic: Once on the way to the suburban altar, with the heir apparent following, he pointed to thorns beside the road and said: "The ancients used these for flogging because they dispel wind; though cold, they do not injure."

sentences.zh: 尚書開濟議法密，諭之曰：「竭澤而漁，害及鯤鮞，焚林而田，禍及麛鷇。

translations.literal: Minister Kai Ji advocated dense law; the emperor admonished him: "Draining the marsh to catch fish harms even minnows and fry; burning the forest to hunt brings calamity even to fawns and nestlings.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Kai Ji urged intricate law; the emperor rebuked him: "Draining a marsh to catch fish destroys even the minnows; burning a forest to hunt kills even the fawns in their nests.

sentences.zh: 法太巧密，民何以自全？」

translations.literal: If the law is too artful and dense, how can the people preserve themselves?"
translations.idiomatic: If the law grows too clever and tight, how can ordinary people survive?"

sentences.zh: 濟慚謝。

translations.literal: Ji ashamedly apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Kai Ji withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 參政楊憲欲重法，帝曰：「求生於重典，猶索魚於釜，得活難矣。」

translations.literal: Participating Secretary Yang Xian wished to use heavy law; the emperor said: "Seeking life under severe statutes is like seeking fish in a cauldron—hardly possible to stay alive."
translations.idiomatic: Participating Secretary Yang Xian wanted heavier penalties; the emperor said: "Seeking life under harsh law is like fishing in a boiling pot—you will hardly keep anyone alive."

sentences.zh: 御史中丞陳寧曰：「法重則人不輕犯，吏察則下無遁情。」

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Chen Ning said: "Heavy law then people do not lightly offend; strict officials then subordinates have no evasions."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Chen Ning said: "Severe law keeps people from offending lightly; vigilant officials leave subordinates no room to hide."

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「不然。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Not so.

sentences.zh: 古人制刑以防惡衛善，故唐、虞畫衣冠、異章服以為戮，而民不犯。

translations.literal: The ancients made punishments to guard against evil and protect the good; therefore Tang and Yu painted clothing and distinguished dress and insignia as shame, and the people did not offend.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients fashioned punishments to repel evil and protect the good. Tang and Yu marked shame with painted garments and distinctive dress, and the people did not offend.

sentences.zh: 秦有鑿顛抽脅之刑、參夷之誅，而囹圄成市，天下怨叛。

translations.literal: Qin had punishments of boring the crown and pulling out ribs and extermination of three clans, yet prisons became marketplaces and all under Heaven resented and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Qin bore holes in skulls, pulled out ribs, and exterminated three clans, yet its prisons filled like marketplaces and the realm turned to rebellion.

sentences.zh: 未聞用商、韓之法，可致堯、舜之治也。」

translations.literal: Never has it been heard that using the laws of Shang and Han could achieve the governance of Yao and Shun."
translations.idiomatic: No one has ever governed like Yao and Shun by applying the laws of Shang Yang and Han Fei."

sentences.zh: 寧慚而退。

translations.literal: Ning ashamedly withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ning withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 又嘗謂尚書劉惟謙曰：「仁義者，養民之膏粱也；

translations.literal: He also once told Minister Liu Weiqian: "Benevolence and righteousness are the fine grain that nourishes the people;
translations.idiomatic: He also once told Minister Liu Weiqian: "Benevolence and righteousness are the grain that nourishes the people;

sentences.zh: 刑罰者，懲惡之藥石也。

translations.literal: punishments are the medicine and stone that punish evil.
translations.idiomatic: punishments are the medicine that punishes evil.

sentences.zh: 舍仁義而專用刑罰，是以藥石養人，豈得謂善治乎？」

translations.literal: To abandon benevolence and righteousness and rely solely on punishments is to nourish people with medicine and stone—can this be called good governance?
translations.idiomatic: To abandon benevolence and rely only on punishment is to feed people medicine instead of food—can that be good governance?

sentences.zh: 蓋太祖用重典以懲一時，而酌中制以垂後世，故猛烈之治，寬仁之詔，相輔而行，未嘗偏廢也。

translations.literal: Thus the Grand Ancestor used severe statutes to punish for a time, yet weighed the mean to establish rules for posterity; therefore fierce governance and lenient edicts proceeded in mutual support, never wholly abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwu emperor used harsh law to shock his age, yet tempered it with moderate institutions for posterity; fierce enforcement and merciful edicts worked together and were never wholly abandoned.

sentences.zh: 建文帝繼體守文，專欲以仁義化民。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen succeeded and maintained culture, wishing exclusively to transform the people through benevolence and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen succeeded to a settled order and sought to transform the people through benevolence and righteousness alone.

sentences.zh: 元年刑部報囚，減太祖時十三矣。

translations.literal: In the first year the Ministry of Punishment reported prisoners, reduced by thirteen parts from the Grand Ancestor's time.
translations.idiomatic: In his first year the Ministry of Punishment reported prisoner numbers down by thirteen parts from Hongwu levels.

sentences.zh: 成祖起靖難之師，悉指忠臣為奸黨，甚者加族誅、掘塚，妻女發浣衣局、教坊司，親黨謫戍者至隆、萬間猶勾伍不絕也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Chengzu raised the army of Jingnan, he pointed to loyal ministers as traitorous factions; in extreme cases he added extermination of clans and disinterment, sent wives and daughters to the Laundry Bureau and the Music Bureau, and banished relatives to frontier service—through the Longqing and Wanli reigns conscription rolls still continued without cease.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle emperor marched under the banner of Jingnan, he labeled loyal ministers traitors; in the worst cases he exterminated clans, dug up graves, sent wives and daughters to the Laundry and Music Bureaus, and banished kin to the frontier—conscription rolls for their descendants continued into Longqing and Wanli.

sentences.zh: 抗違者既盡殺戮，懼人竊議之，疾誹謗特甚。

translations.literal: After those who resisted were wholly slaughtered, fearing people would privately discuss it, he was especially severe on slander.
translations.idiomatic: Once dissenters were killed, he feared whispers against him and grew especially harsh toward slander.

sentences.zh: 山陽民丁鈺訐其鄉誹謗，罪數十人。

translations.literal: Ding Yu of Shanyang accused his township of slander, and several dozen were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Yu of Shanyang denounced his neighbors for slander, and dozens were punished.

sentences.zh: 法司迎上旨，言鈺纔可用，立命為刑科給事中。

translations.literal: The judicial offices, welcoming the emperor's intent, said Yu was barely usable and immediately appointed him supervising secretary of the Penal Affairs Section.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial offices, reading the emperor's mood, declared Yu barely usable and immediately made him a Penal Affairs supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 永樂十七年，復申其禁。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Yongle, the prohibition was again proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 17 the prohibition was proclaimed again.

sentences.zh: 而陳瑛、呂震、紀綱輩先後用事，專以刻深固寵。

translations.literal: Yet Chen Ying, Lü Zhen, Ji Gang, and others in succession held power, relying exclusively on severity and harshness to secure favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chen Ying, Lü Zhen, Ji Gang, and others held power in turn, securing favor through cruelty and severity.

sentences.zh: 於是蕭議、周新、解縉等多無罪死。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xiao Yi, Zhou Xin, Xie Jin, and many others died without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yi, Zhou Xin, Xie Jin, and many others died innocent.

sentences.zh: 然帝心知苛法之非，間示寬大。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor in his heart knew harsh law was wrong and occasionally showed leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor knew harsh law was wrong and sometimes showed mercy.

sentences.zh: 千戶某灌桐油皮鞭中以決人，刑部當以杖，命並罷其職。

translations.literal: A thousand-household commander stuffed tung-oil skin into a whip to decide cases; the Ministry of Punishment proposed bamboo punishment, and the emperor ordered his office abolished as well.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand-household commander hid tung-oil skin inside a whip to beat prisoners; the Ministry proposed bamboo punishment, and the emperor stripped him of office as well.

sentences.zh: 法司奏冒支官糧者，命即戮之，刑部為覆奏。

translations.literal: The judicial offices memorialized those who falsely drew official grain; the emperor ordered immediate execution, and the Ministry of Punishment submitted a rehearing memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When the judicial offices reported officials who falsely drew government grain, the emperor ordered immediate execution; the Ministry of Punishment reheard the case.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此朕一時之怒，過矣，其依律。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This was my momentary anger—it went too far; follow the law.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "That was a moment of anger—it went too far. Follow the law.

sentences.zh: 自今犯罪皆五覆奏。」

translations.literal: Henceforth for all crimes use five rehearing memorials."
translations.idiomatic: From now on, every capital case requires five rehearings."

sentences.zh: 至仁宗性甚仁恕，甫即位，謂金純、劉觀曰：「卿等皆國大臣，如朕處法失中，須更執奏，朕不難從善也。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong acceded, he was very benevolent and forgiving; just upon taking the throne he told Jin Chun and Liu Guan: "You are all great ministers of the state; if my handling of law misses the mean, you must again submit and report; I am not hard put to follow what is good."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong was deeply merciful. On accession he told Jin Chun and Liu Guan: "You are state ministers; if my judgments miss the mark, press your objections—I am not unwilling to do better."

sentences.zh: 因召學士楊士奇、楊榮、金幼孜至榻前，諭曰：「比年法司之濫，朕豈不知。

translations.literal: He then summoned Academicians Yang Shiqi, Yang Rong, and Jin Youzi to the couch and instructed: "In recent years the abuse of the judicial offices—I know it well.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Academicians Yang Shiqi, Yang Rong, and Jin Youzi and said: "I know well how the judicial offices have been abused.

sentences.zh: 其所擬大逆不道，往往出於文致，先帝數切戒之。

translations.literal: What they proposed as great treason and disloyalty often came from textual fabrication; the former emperor repeatedly sternly warned against this.
translations.idiomatic: Charges of great treason were often fabricated on paper; my father warned against this again and again.

sentences.zh: 故死刑必四五覆奏，而法司略不加意，甘為酷吏而不愧。

translations.literal: Therefore for death sentences there must be four or five rehearing memorials, yet the judicial offices paid little heed, willingly serving as cruel officials without shame.
translations.idiomatic: That is why death sentences require four or five rehearings, yet the courts ignore the rule and serve as cruel officials without shame.

sentences.zh: 自今審重囚，卿三人必往同讞，有冤抑者，雖細故必以聞。」

translations.literal: Henceforth in reviewing grave prisoners, you three must go jointly to deliberate; where there is wrongful suppression, even in small matters you must report.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth when grave prisoners are reviewed, you three must attend jointly; report even small signs of injustice.

sentences.zh: 洪熙改元，二月諭都御史劉觀、大理卿虞謙曰：「往者法司以誣陷為功，人或片言及國事，輒論誹謗，身家破滅，莫復辨理。

translations.literal: In the second month of the Hongxi reign change, he instructed Censor-in-Chief Liu Guan and Court of Judicial Review Director Yu Qian: "Formerly the judicial offices took framing as achievement; if a man in a single phrase touched on state affairs, they judged slander, families were ruined, and none could argue again.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongxi 1, second month, he told Censor-in-Chief Liu Guan and Court Director Yu Qian: "The courts once treated framing as merit; one careless phrase about state affairs became slander, families were destroyed, and no one could recover.

sentences.zh: 今數月間，此風又萌。

translations.literal: Within a few months this wind sprouted again.
translations.idiomatic: Within months the old habit was sprouting again.

sentences.zh: 夫治道所急者求言，所患者以言為諱，奈何禁誹謗哉？」

translations.literal: What the way of governance urgently seeks is to obtain speech; what it fears is treating speech as taboo—how can slander be forbidden?"
translations.idiomatic: Good government needs speech, not silence—how can slander be forbidden?"

sentences.zh: 因顧士奇等曰：「此事必以詔書行之。」

translations.literal: He then turned to Shiqi and others: "This matter must be carried out by edict."
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Shiqi and said: "This must be done by edict."

sentences.zh: 於是士奇承旨，載帝言於己丑詔書云：「若朕一時過於嫉惡，律外用籍沒及淩遲之刑者，法司再三執奏，三奏不允至五，五奏不允，同三公及大臣執奏，必允乃已，永為定制。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shiqi received the order and recorded the emperor's words in the edict of the jichou day: "If I in a moment exceed in hatred and use beyond statute confiscation and dismemberment, the judicial offices must repeatedly submit and report; if three submissions are not accepted, up to five; if five are not accepted, jointly submit with the three dukes and great ministers; it must be accepted before stopping—forever fixed as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi drafted the jichou edict: "If in a fit of hatred I order confiscation or dismemberment beyond statute, the courts must rehear; if three rehearings fail, go to five; if five fail, rehear jointly with the chief ministers—execution waits until approval. This is permanent law.

sentences.zh: 文武諸司亦毋得暴酷用鞭背等刑，及擅用宮刑絕人嗣續。

translations.literal: Civil and military offices also must not cruelly use back-flogging and the like, nor on their own authority use palace punishment to cut off heirs.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military offices must not cruelly flog prisoners' backs or impose palace castration to cut off heirs.

sentences.zh: 有自宮者以不孝論。

translations.literal: Those who castrate themselves are judged unfilial.
translations.idiomatic: Self-castration is judged unfilial.

sentences.zh: 除謀反及大逆者，餘犯止坐本身，毋一切用連坐法。

translations.literal: Apart from conspiracy and great treason, other offenses punish only the offender himself—do not universally apply collective punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Except for conspiracy and great treason, punish only the offender—do not extend guilt by association.

sentences.zh: 告誹謗者勿治。」

translations.literal: Those who accuse others of slander are not prosecuted."
translations.idiomatic: Accusers of slander are not to be prosecuted."

sentences.zh: 在位未一年，仁恩該洽矣。

translations.literal: He reigned less than one year, yet benevolence and grace pervaded.
translations.idiomatic: He reigned less than a year, yet mercy pervaded the realm.

sentences.zh: 宣宗承之，益多惠政。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong succeeded him and further added many benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong succeeded him and added many humane policies.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年，大理寺駁正猗氏民妻王骨都殺夫之冤，帝切責刑官，尚書金純等謝罪，乃已。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuande, the Court of Judicial Review corrected the injustice of Wang Gudu of Yishi, whose wife had killed her husband; the emperor sternly rebuked the penal officials, and Ministers Jin Chun and others apologized before it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 1 the Court of Judicial Review overturned the wrongful conviction of Wang Gudu of Yishi for killing her husband; the emperor rebuked the penal officials sharply until Ministers Jin Chun and others apologized.

sentences.zh: 義勇軍士閻羣兒等九人被誣為盜，當斬，家人擊登聞鼓訴冤。

translations.literal: Nine volunteer soldiers including Yan Qun'er were falsely accused as robbers and due for execution; their families struck the Drum of Direct Appeal pleading injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Nine volunteer soldiers including Yan Qun'er were falsely accused of robbery and condemned to death; their families beat the Drum of Direct Appeal.

sentences.zh: 覆按實不為盜。

translations.literal: Reinvestigation showed they were indeed not robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Reinvestigation proved they were not robbers.

sentences.zh: 命釋羣兒等，而切責都御史劉觀。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered release of Qun'er and the others, and sternly rebuked Censor-in-Chief Liu Guan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor freed Yan Qun'er and the others and sharply rebuked Censor-in-Chief Liu Guan.

sentences.zh: 其後每遇奏囚，色慘然，禦膳為廢。

translations.literal: Thereafter whenever prisoners were reported, his countenance was grim and imperial meals were suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, whenever capital cases were reported, his face darkened and he skipped meals.

sentences.zh: 或以手撤其牘，謂左右曰：「說與刑官少緩之。」

translations.literal: Sometimes he personally tore up the memorial and told those beside him: "Tell the penal officials to go a little slower."
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he tore up the memorial himself and told attendants: "Tell the penal officials to slow down."

sentences.zh: 一日，禦文華殿與羣臣論古肉刑，侍臣對：「漢除肉刑，人遂輕犯法。」

translations.literal: One day in the Wenhua Hall he discussed with the multitude of officials ancient corporal punishments; attending ministers replied: "When Han abolished corporal punishment, people then lightly violated law.
translations.idiomatic: One day in Wenhua Hall he discussed ancient corporal punishments with his ministers; they replied: "When Han abolished corporal punishment, people took the law lightly.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此自由教化，豈關肉刑之有無。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This lies in teaching and transformation—what relation has it to whether corporal punishment exists or not?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "That depends on education, not on whether corporal punishment exists.

sentences.zh: 舜法有流宥金贖，而四凶之罪止於竄殛。

translations.literal: Shun's law had exile, pardon, and redemption by metal, yet the crimes of the Four Villains ended only in banishment and execution.
translations.idiomatic: Shun's law allowed exile, pardon, and redemption with metal, yet the Four Villains were only banished or executed.

sentences.zh: 可見當時被肉刑者，必皆重罪，不濫及也。

translations.literal: Thus it can be seen that those who received corporal punishment at the time were certainly all grave offenses, not broadly extended.
translations.idiomatic: Those who suffered corporal punishment then were surely grave offenders, not victims of indiscriminate application.

sentences.zh: 況漢承秦敝，挾書有律，若概用肉刑，受傷者必多矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover Han inherited Qin's abuses; there was law against possessing books—if corporal punishment were applied universally, the injured would certainly be many.
translations.idiomatic: Han inherited Qin's harshness and even punished book possession; universal corporal punishment would have maimed countless people.

sentences.zh: 明年，著《帝訓》五十五篇，其一恤刑也。

translations.literal: The next year he compiled the fifty-five articles of Imperial Instructions, one of which concerned sparing punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he issued the fifty-five articles of Imperial Instructions, including one on merciful punishment.

sentences.zh: 武進伯硃冕言：「比遣舍人林寬等送囚百十七人戍邊，到者僅五十人，餘皆道死。」

translations.literal: Military Commander Zhu Mian said: "Recently housemen Lin Kuan and others escorted one hundred seventeen prisoners to border service; only fifty arrived—the rest all died on the road."
translations.idiomatic: Commander Zhu Mian reported: "Recently Lin Kuan and others escorted 117 prisoners to the frontier; only 50 arrived—the rest died on the road."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命法司窮治之。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged and ordered the judicial offices to investigate thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered a full investigation.

sentences.zh: 帝寬詔歲下，閱囚屢決遣，有至三千人者。

translations.literal: The emperor's lenient edicts came down each year; reviewing prisoners he repeatedly decided and released them, sometimes reaching three thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Lenient edicts came every year; reviewing prisoners, he repeatedly released them—sometimes as many as three thousand.

sentences.zh: 諭刑官曰：「吾慮其瘐死，故寬貸之，非常制也。」

translations.literal: He instructed the penal officials: "I fear they die of illness in prison—therefore I leniently pardon them; this is not the ordinary system.
translations.idiomatic: He told penal officials: "I fear prisoners die in custody—that is why I pardon them; this is not ordinary practice.

sentences.zh: 是時，官吏納米百石若五十石，得贖雜犯死罪，軍民減十之二。

translations.literal: At that time officials who contributed one hundred or fifty shi of grain could redeem miscellaneous capital offenses; soldiers and civilians had two parts in ten reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who contributed 100 or 50 shi of grain could redeem miscellaneous capital offenses; soldiers and civilians received a two-tenths reduction.

sentences.zh: 諸邊衛十二石，遼東二十石，於例為太輕，然獨嚴贓吏之罰。

translations.literal: Border garrisons required twelve shi, Liaodong twenty shi—lighter by precedent—yet only penalties for corrupt officials were strict.
translations.idiomatic: Border garrisons required 12 shi, Liaodong 20—lighter by precedent—yet penalties for corrupt officials alone remained strict.

sentences.zh: 命文職犯贓者俱依律科斷。

translations.literal: An order provided that civil officials who committed bribery offenses were all sentenced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: An order required civil officials convicted of bribery to be sentenced strictly by law.

sentences.zh: 由是用法輕，而貪墨之風亦不甚恣，然明制重朋比之誅。

translations.literal: Thus law was used lightly, yet the wind of greed and corruption did not greatly run wild; yet Ming institutions heavily punished factional collusion.
translations.idiomatic: Law was applied lightly overall, and corruption did not run rampant; yet Ming law punished factional collusion severely.

sentences.zh: 都御史夏迪催糧常州，御史何楚英誣以受金。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Xia Di pressed grain collection in Changzhou; Censor He Chuying falsely accused him of receiving gold.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Xia Di pressed grain collection in Changzhou; Censor He Chuying falsely accused him of taking gold.

sentences.zh: 諸司懼罪，明知其冤，不敢白，迪竟充驛夫憤死。

translations.literal: The various offices feared guilt, clearly knowing his injustice yet dared not speak; Di finally died in anger as a postal relay worker.
translations.idiomatic: Offices fearing punishment knew he was innocent but dared not speak; Xia Di died in anger as a postal relay worker.

sentences.zh: 以帝之寬仁，而大臣有冤死者，此立法之弊也。

translations.literal: Though the emperor was lenient and benevolent, yet great ministers died wrongfully—this was a flaw of legislation.
translations.idiomatic: Even under a lenient emperor, a great minister died wrongfully—a flaw in the law itself.

sentences.zh: 英宗以後，仁、宣之政衰。

translations.literal: After Emperor Yingzong, the policies of Renzong and Xuanzong declined.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yingzong, the humane policies of Renzong and Xuanzong faded.

sentences.zh: 正統初，三楊當國，猶恪守祖法，禁內外諸司鍛煉刑獄。

translations.literal: In early Zhengtong, the Three Yangs held state power and still strictly kept ancestral law, forbidding inner and outer offices from forging and refining prison cases.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengtong the Three Yangs still upheld ancestral law and forbade inner and outer offices from fabricating prison cases.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書魏源以災旱上疑獄，請命各巡撫審錄。

translations.literal: Minister of Punishment Wei Yuan, because of drought, submitted doubtful cases and requested that each grand coordinator review and record them.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wei Yuan, citing drought, submitted doubtful cases and asked each grand coordinator to review them.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 無巡撫者命巡按。

translations.literal: Where there was no grand coordinator, the touring inspector was ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Where no grand coordinator existed, a touring inspector was assigned.

sentences.zh: 清軍御史、行在都察院亦以疑獄上，通審錄之。

translations.literal: The army-inspection censor and the Nanjing Censorate also submitted doubtful cases for joint review and recording.
translations.idiomatic: Army-inspection censors and the Nanjing Censorate also submitted doubtful cases for joint review.

sentences.zh: 御史陳祚言：「法司論獄，多違定律，專務刻深。

translations.literal: Censor Chen Zuo said: "The judicial offices in deciding cases often violated fixed statutes, exclusively pursuing severity.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Chen Zuo said: "The courts often violate fixed statutes and pursue severity for its own sake.

sentences.zh: 如戶部侍郎吳璽舉淫行主事吳軏，宜坐貢舉非其人罪，乃加以奏事有規避律斬。

translations.literal: For example, Vice Minister of Revenue Wu Xi reported Chief Clerk Wu Yue for licentious conduct; he should have been sentenced for recommending an unfit person, yet they added the statute on memorializing with evasion and sentenced to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Wu Xi reported Chief Clerk Wu Yue for misconduct; the proper charge was recommending an unfit person, yet the courts added a statute on evasive memorializing and sought decapitation.

sentences.zh: 及軏自經死，獄官卒之罪，明有遞減科，乃援不應為事理重者，概杖之。

translations.literal: When Yue hanged himself, the prison official's offense for letting a prisoner die clearly had a statute of progressive reduction, yet they cited "doing what ought not to be done, serious in principle" and generally beat them with bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Yue hanged himself, the jailer's offense had a clear statute of progressive reduction, yet the courts cited "serious impropriety" and flogged everyone.

sentences.zh: 夫原情以定律，祖宗防範至周，而法司乃抑輕從重至此，非所以廣聖朝之仁厚也。

translations.literal: To examine the circumstances and fix the law—the ancestral founders' guard was thorough—yet the judicial offices suppressed the light and followed the heavy to this extent; this is not how to extend the sage court's benevolence and generosity.
translations.idiomatic: The founders guarded against this thoroughly, yet the courts now escalate mild cases into harsh ones—this does not extend the dynasty's benevolence.

sentences.zh: 今後有妄援重律者，請以變亂成法罪之。」

translations.literal: Henceforth where heavy statutes are rashly invoked, I request sentencing for the crime of disturbing established law."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth anyone who rashly invokes heavy statutes should be punished for disturbing established law."

sentences.zh: 帝是其言，為申警戒。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words and issued a warning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and issued a warning.

sentences.zh: 至六年，王振始亂政，數辱廷臣，刑章大紊。

translations.literal: By the sixth year Wang Zhen began to disorder government, repeatedly humiliating court ministers; penal provisions were greatly confused.
translations.idiomatic: By the sixth year Wang Zhen began to corrupt government, humiliating court ministers and throwing penal law into chaos.

sentences.zh: 侍講劉球條上十事，中言：「天降災譴，多感於刑罰之不中。

translations.literal: Reader-in-Waiting Liu Qiu submitted ten items, among which he said: "Heaven sends disaster and reproof, much stirred by punishments missing the mean.
translations.idiomatic: Reader-in-Waiting Liu Qiu submitted ten reforms, saying: "Heaven's disasters often reflect unjust punishments.

sentences.zh: 宜一任法司，視其徇私不當者而加以罪。

translations.literal: It is fitting to leave all to the judicial offices, and where they act with private partiality and impropriety, add guilt upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Leave judgment to the courts, and punish officials who decide with partiality.

sentences.zh: 雖有觸忤，如漢犯蹕盜環之事，猶當聽張釋之之執奏而從之。」

translations.literal: Even if there is offense against the throne, as in Han's case of violating the imperial procession and stealing the ring, still one should listen to Zhang Shizhi's resolute submission and follow it."
translations.idiomatic: Even when a subject offends the throne—as in Han times when someone violated the imperial procession and stole a ring—the emperor should still heed a minister's firm remonstrance, as Zhang Shizhi's was heeded."

sentences.zh: 帝不能用。

translations.literal: The emperor could not use it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not adopt the proposal.

sentences.zh: 而球即以是疏觸振怒，死於獄。

translations.literal: Yet Qiu because of this memorial provoked Zhen's anger and died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiu's memorial provoked Wang Zhen's wrath, and he died in prison.

sentences.zh: 然諸酷虐事，大率振為之，帝心頗寬平。

translations.literal: Yet for all cruel and abusive matters, largely Zhen did them; the emperor's heart was rather lenient and even.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the cruelty came from Wang Zhen; the emperor himself remained relatively mild.

sentences.zh: 十一年，大理卿俞士悅以毆鬥殺人之類百餘人聞，請宥，俱減死戍邊。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Court of Judicial Review Director Yu Shiyue, hearing of more than one hundred cases of brawling and killing and the like, requested pardon; all were reduced from death to border service.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, Court Director Yu Shiyue, hearing of more than a hundred brawling-and-killing cases, asked for mercy; all were reduced from death to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 景泰中，陽谷主簿馬彥斌當斬，其子震請代死。

translations.literal: In the Jingtai period, Yanggu Chief Clerk Ma Yanbin was due for decapitation; his son Zhen requested to die in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jingtai, Yanggu chief clerk Ma Yanbin was condemned to death; his son Zhen asked to die in his place.

sentences.zh: 特宥彥斌，編震充邊衛軍。

translations.literal: He was specially pardoned Yanbin and enrolled Zhen as a border-garrison soldier.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbin was specially pardoned, and Zhen was enrolled as a frontier soldier.

sentences.zh: 大理少卿薛瑄曰：「法司發擬罪囚，多加參語奏請，變亂律意。」

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Xue Xuan said: "The judicial offices in proposing sentences for prisoners often added commentary language in memorials, disturbing the intent of the statutes."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Xue Xuan said: "The courts often add commentary when proposing sentences, distorting the statutes."

sentences.zh: 詔法官問獄，一依律令，不許妄加參語。

translations.literal: An edict ordered judges in interrogating prisons to follow statutes and orders exclusively, not permitting rash addition of commentary.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered judges to follow statutes exactly and not add commentary.

sentences.zh: 六年，以災異審錄中外刑獄，全活者甚眾。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, because of calamities and portents, cases within and without were reviewed and recorded; those wholly spared were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, portents prompted review of cases nationwide, and many lives were spared.

sentences.zh: 天順中，詔獄繁興，三法司、錦衣獄多繫囚未決，吏往往泄獄情為奸。

translations.literal: In the Tianshun period, prison cases flourished; the Three Judicial Offices and Embroidered Uniform Guard prisons held many prisoners undecided, and clerks often leaked prison information for wicked ends.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianshun, prison cases multiplied; the Three Judicial Offices and Embroidered Uniform Guard held many unresolved prisoners, and clerks often leaked case information for profit.

sentences.zh: 都御史蕭維楨附會徐有貞，枉殺王文、于謙等。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Xiao Weizhen attached himself to Xu Youzhen and wrongly killed Wang Wen, Yu Qian, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Xiao Weizhen joined Xu Youzhen in the wrongful execution of Wang Wen, Yu Qian, and others.

sentences.zh: 而刑部侍郎劉廣衡即以詐撰制文，坐有貞斬罪。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Punishment Liu Guangheng was because of falsely drafting an imperial document sentenced with Youzhen to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Liu Guangheng was condemned to death with Xu Youzhen for forging an imperial document.

sentences.zh: 其後緹騎四出，海內不安。

translations.literal: Thereafter imperial guards rode out in all directions and the realm was unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward imperial guards rode out everywhere, and the realm grew unsettled.

sentences.zh: 然霜降後審錄重囚，實自天順間始。

translations.literal: Yet review and recording of grave prisoners after frost descent in truth began in the Tianshun period.
translations.idiomatic: Review of capital cases after Frost Descent in fact began under Tianshun.

sentences.zh: 至成化初，刑部尚書陸瑜等以請，命舉行之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua, Minister of Punishment Lu Yu and others requested on memorial; an order was issued to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chenghua, Minister Lu Yu and others memorialized for the practice, and an order carried it out.

sentences.zh: 獄上，杖其情可矜疑者，免死發戍。

translations.literal: Prisoners reported upward, those whose circumstances were pitiable or doubtful were beaten with the light bamboo and exempted from death, sent to border service.
translations.idiomatic: Cases reported upward: prisoners whose circumstances were doubtful or pitiable received light bamboo and were spared death for frontier service.

sentences.zh: 列代奉行，人獲沾法外恩矣。

translations.literal: Successive reigns carried it out; people obtained grace beyond the law.
translations.idiomatic: Later reigns followed the practice, and many received mercy beyond what statute allowed.

sentences.zh: 憲宗之即位也，敕三法司：「中外文武羣臣除贓罪外，所犯罪名紀錄在官者，悉與湔滌。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong acceded, he instructed the Three Judicial Offices: "Civil and military officials throughout, apart from bribery offenses, all crime records kept in office shall be entirely cleansed."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong acceded, he ordered the Three Judicial Offices: "Except for bribery, wipe clean every official crime record on file."

sentences.zh: 其後歲以為常。

translations.literal: Thereafter this was done each year as routine.
translations.idiomatic: The cleansing became an annual routine.

sentences.zh: 十年，當決囚，冬至節近，特命過節行刑。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, when prisoners were due for execution, the winter solstice was near; a special order permitted execution after the festival.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, with executions due and the winter solstice near, a special order allowed execution after the festival.

sentences.zh: 既而給事中言，冬至後行刑非時，遂詔俟來年冬月。

translations.literal: Thereafter Supervising Secretaries said that execution after the winter solstice was untimely, and an edict ordered waiting until the winter month of the coming year.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries then argued that post-solstice execution was untimely, and an edict postponed cases until the next winter.

sentences.zh: 山西巡撫何喬新劾奏遲延獄詞僉事尚敬、劉源，因言：「凡二司不決斷詞訟者，半年之上，悉宜奏請執問。」

translations.literal: Shanxi Grand Coordinator He Qiaoxin impeached and memorialized Vice Commissioners Shang Jing and Liu Yuan for delaying case documents, and further said: "For all litigation undecided by the two commissions for more than half a year, all should memorialize and request enforced interrogation."
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi Grand Coordinator He Qiaoxin impeached Vice Commissioners Shang Jing and Liu Yuan for delaying cases and proposed: "Any lawsuit undecided for half a year should be reported for enforced interrogation."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「刑獄重事，《周書》曰：『要囚，服念五六日至於旬時』，特為未得其情者言耳。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Prison cases are weighty matters; the Book of Zhou says: 'For doubtful prisoners, ponder five or six days up to ten days'—this speaks specifically of those whose circumstances have not yet been obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Prison cases are grave. The Book of Zhou says doubtful prisoners should be pondered five or six days up to ten—meaning cases whose facts are not yet clear.

sentences.zh: 苟得其情，即宜決斷。

translations.literal: If the circumstances are obtained, then it is fitting to decide.
translations.idiomatic: Once the facts are clear, judgment should follow at once.

sentences.zh: 無罪拘幽，往往瘐死，是刑官殺之也。

translations.literal: The innocent detained in secret often die of illness in prison—this is the penal officials killing them.
translations.idiomatic: Innocent people detained too long often die in custody—that is judicial murder.

sentences.zh: 故律特著淹禁罪囚之條，其即以喬新所奏，通行天下。」

translations.literal: Therefore the code specially sets forth the article on excessive detention of prisoners; immediately take He Qiaoxin's memorial and extend it throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the code penalizes excessive detention. Issue He Qiaoxin's proposal throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 又定制，凡盜賊贓仗未真、人命死傷未經勘驗、輒加重刑致死獄中者，審勘有無故失明白，不分軍民職官，俱視酷刑事例為民。

translations.literal: Another regulation was set: wherever stolen goods and weapons were not verified, or deaths and injuries were not examined, and heavy punishment was rashly added causing death in prison—if investigation showed whether there was intent or negligence clearly, regardless of soldier, civilian, or official, all were treated by the precedent for cruel officials and reduced to commoners.
