translations.idiomatic: Another rule punished officials who imposed heavy torture before stolen goods or corpses were verified and thereby caused deaths in custody; whether soldier, civilian, or official, they were reduced to commoner status like other cruel judges.

sentences.zh: 侍郎楊宣妻悍妒，殺婢十餘人，部擬命婦合坐者律，特命決杖五十。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Yang Xuan's wife was fierce and jealous and killed more than ten maidservants; the ministry proposed the statute on wives jointly sitting for husbands; a special order decided fifty blows of the heavy bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Yang Xuan's jealous wife killed more than ten maidservants; the ministry proposed joint punishment for wives; a special order imposed fifty blows of the heavy bamboo.

sentences.zh: 時帝多裨政，而於刑獄尤慎之，所失惟一二事。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor had many good supplementary policies, yet was especially careful in prison cases; his errors were only one or two matters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued many good reforms and was especially cautious in criminal matters; his mistakes were few.

sentences.zh: 嘗欲殺一囚，不許覆奏。

translations.literal: Once he wished to kill a prisoner and did not permit rehearing memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Once he wished to execute a prisoner and refused rehearing.

sentences.zh: 御史方佑復以請，帝怒，杖謫佑。

translations.literal: Censor Fang You again requested on memorial; the emperor was angry and beat and banished You.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Fang You petitioned again; the emperor was angry, beat him, and banished him.

sentences.zh: 吉安知府許總有罪，中官黃高嗾法司論斬。

translations.literal: Ji'an Prefect Xu Zong had guilt; eunuch Huang Gao incited the judicial offices to propose decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Ji'an Prefect Xu Zong was guilty; eunuch Huang Gao urged the courts to seek decapitation.

sentences.zh: 給事中白昂以未經審錄為請，不聽，竟乘夜斬之。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Bai Ang requested because he had not yet undergone examination and recording; the emperor did not listen, and in the end executed him by night.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Bai Ang pleaded that Xu had not yet been fully examined; the emperor refused and had him executed by night.

sentences.zh: 孝宗初立，免應決死罪四十八人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong first acceded, he pardoned forty-eight men due for execution.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong acceded, he pardoned forty-eight men awaiting execution.

sentences.zh: 元年，知州劉概坐妖言罪斬，以王恕爭，得長系。

translations.literal: In the first year, Prefect Liu Gai was sentenced to decapitation for heterodox speech; because Wang Su contended, he was long imprisoned instead.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year, Prefect Liu Gai was condemned for heterodox speech; Wang Su's protest kept him imprisoned instead of executed.

sentences.zh: 末年，刑部尚書閔珪讞重獄，忤旨，久不下。

translations.literal: In his late years, Minister of Punishment Min Gui deliberated a grave case, offended the imperial intent, and long went undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the reign, Minister Min Gui deliberated a grave case, offended the emperor, and the decision lingered.

sentences.zh: 帝與劉大夏語及之，對曰：「人臣執法效忠，珪所為無足異。」

translations.literal: The emperor spoke of it with Liu Daxia, who replied: "A minister enforcing law in loyal service—Gui's conduct is not greatly different."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor discussed it with Liu Daxia, who said: "A minister enforcing law in loyal service—Min Gui has done nothing unusual."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「且道自古君臣曾有此事否？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Yet tell me—from antiquity have ruler and minister ever had such a matter?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "Has any ruler and minister ever had such a standoff?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣幼讀《孟子》，見瞽瞍殺人，皋陶執之語。

translations.literal: Daxia replied: "Your servant in youth read the Mencius and saw the passage where Blind Old Man kills a man and Gao Yao arrests him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daxia replied: "I read Mencius as a boy—the passage where Blind Old Man kills a man and Gao Yao arrests him.

sentences.zh: 珪所執，未可深責也。」

translations.literal: What Gui enforced cannot be deeply blamed."
translations.idiomatic: Min Gui's enforcement cannot be deeply faulted."

sentences.zh: 帝頷之。

translations.literal: The emperor nodded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded.

sentences.zh: 明日疏下，遂如擬。

translations.literal: The next day the memorial was issued downward and followed the proposal as deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the memorial came down approving Min Gui's proposal.

sentences.zh: 前後所任司寇何喬新、彭韶、白昂、閔珪皆持法平者，海內翕然頌仁德焉。

translations.literal: Before and after, the ministers of punishment appointed—He Qiaoxin, Peng Shao, Bai Ang, and Min Gui—were all even-handed in holding law; throughout the realm they uniformly praised benevolent virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers of punishment under Xiaozong—He Qiaoxin, Peng Shao, Bai Ang, and Min Gui—held the law evenly, and the realm praised the emperor's benevolence.

sentences.zh: 正德五年會審重囚，減死者二人。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengde, joint review of grave prisoners reduced two from death.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 5, joint review of capital prisoners reduced two death sentences.

sentences.zh: 時冤濫滿獄，李東陽等因風霾以為言，特許寬恤。

translations.literal: At the time wrongful imprisonment filled the prisons; Li Dongyang and others, taking sandstorms as occasion, spoke of it; a special order permitted leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Prisons were full of wrongful convictions; Li Dongyang and others cited sandstorms to plead for mercy, and a special order granted leniency.

sentences.zh: 而刑官懼觸劉瑾怒，所上止此。

translations.literal: Yet the penal officials feared provoking Liu Jin's anger; what they reported upward stopped at this.
translations.idiomatic: Penal officials feared Liu Jin's wrath and reported only these two reductions.

sentences.zh: 後磔流賊趙鐩等於市，剝為魁者六人皮。

translations.literal: Later the bandit Zhao Zhan was dismembered in the market; the skins of six ringleaders were flayed.
translations.idiomatic: Later the bandit Zhao Zhan was dismembered in the market, and six ringleaders were flayed.

sentences.zh: 法司奏祖訓有禁，不聽。

translations.literal: The judicial offices memorialized that ancestral instruction forbade this; the emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The courts cited ancestral prohibition; the emperor ignored them.

sentences.zh: 尋以皮製鞍鐙，帝每騎乘之。

translations.literal: Soon the skins were made into saddle stirrups; the emperor rode using them each time.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the skins were made into saddle stirrups, which the emperor used when riding.

sentences.zh: 而廷杖直言之臣，亦武宗為甚。

translations.literal: Beating court ministers who spoke directly was also most severe under Emperor Wuzong.
translations.idiomatic: Court beatings of outspoken ministers were also harshest under Emperor Wuzong.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位七月，因日精門災，疏理冤抑，命再問緩死者三十八人，而廖鵬、王瓛、齊佐等與焉。

translations.literal: In the seventh month after Emperor Shizong acceded, because of disaster at the Rijing Gate, he ordered review of wrongful suppressions and commanded re-interrogation of thirty-eight men due for delayed death, among them Liao Peng, Wang Fan, Qi Zuo, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Seven months after the Jiajing emperor acceded, fire at the Rijing Gate prompted review of wrongful convictions; thirty-eight men awaiting execution were re-examined, including Liao Peng, Wang Fan, and Qi Zuo.

sentences.zh: 給事中李復禮等言：「鵬等皆江彬、強尼之黨。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Li Fuli and others said: "Peng and others are all partisans of Jiang Bin and the strong monks.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretaries Li Fuli and others said: "Liao Peng and the others are Jiang Bin's faction.

sentences.zh: 王法所必誅。」

translations.literal: Wang's law must certainly execute them."
translations.idiomatic: The law requires their execution."

sentences.zh: 乃令禁之如故。

translations.literal: They were ordered held as before.
translations.idiomatic: They were ordered held as before.

sentences.zh: 後皆次第伏法。

translations.literal: Later all in succession suffered execution according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Later they were all executed in turn.

sentences.zh: 自杖諸爭大禮者，遂痛折廷臣。

translations.literal: From beating the multitude disputing the Great Rites, he then bitterly broke court ministers.
translations.idiomatic: After beating ministers who disputed the Great Rites, he broke the court ever more harshly.

sentences.zh: 六年，命張璁、桂萼、方獻夫攝三法司，變李福達之獄，欲坐馬錄以奸黨律。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he ordered Zhang Cong, Gui E, and Fang Xianfu to administer the Three Judicial Offices and change the Li Fuda case, wishing to sentence Ma Lu under the traitorous faction statute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he ordered Zhang Cong, Gui E, and Fang Xianfu to take over the Three Judicial Offices, reverse the Li Fuda case, and condemn Ma Lu under the traitorous faction statute.

sentences.zh: 楊一清力爭，乃戍錄，而坐罪者四十餘人。

translations.literal: Yang Yiqing contended forcefully; Lu was banished to service and more than forty were sentenced.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yiqing protested fiercely; Ma Lu was exiled and more than forty were punished.

sentences.zh: 璁等以為己功，遂請帝編《欽明大獄錄》頒示天下。

translations.literal: Cong and others took it as their achievement and then requested the emperor compile the Record of Imperially Clarified Great Cases and promulgate it throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong and the others claimed credit and asked the emperor to compile the Record of Imperially Clarified Great Cases and publish it nationwide.

sentences.zh: 是獄所坐，大抵璁三人夙嫌者。

translations.literal: Those implicated in this case were largely the three men's old grudges.
translations.idiomatic: Most of those implicated were old enemies of the three men.

sentences.zh: 以祖宗之法，供權臣排陷，而帝不悟也。

translations.literal: Using the ancestral founders' law to serve factional framing, yet the emperor did not perceive it.
translations.idiomatic: They used ancestral law to settle private scores, and the emperor did not see it.

sentences.zh: 八年，京師民張福殺母，訴為張柱所殺，刑部郎中魏應召覆治得實。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, commoner Zhang Fu of the capital killed his mother and claimed Zhang Zhu killed her; Ministry Bureau Director Wei Yingzhao reinvestigated and obtained the truth.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, Beijing commoner Zhang Fu killed his mother and blamed Zhang Zhu; Bureau Director Wei Yingzhao reinvestigated and found the truth.

sentences.zh: 而帝以柱乃武宗後家僕，有意曲殺之，命侍郎許訁贊盡反讞詞，而下都御史熊浹及應召於獄。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor, because Zhu was a household servant of the late Wuzong's consort's family, intended to kill him by bias; he ordered Vice Minister Xu Xun to endorse fully reversing the deliberation and sent Censor-in-Chief Xiong Xian and Yingzhao to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhu was a servant of the late Wuzong's consort's family, the emperor wished to kill him by bias; he ordered Vice Minister Xu Xun to reverse the verdict and imprisoned Censor-in-Chief Xiong Xian and Wei Yingzhao.

sentences.zh: 其後，猜忌日甚，冤濫者多，雖間命寬恤，而意主苛刻。

translations.literal: Thereafter suspicion grew daily; wrongful imprisonment was many; though occasionally orders for leniency were issued, the intent chiefly remained harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Suspicion deepened daily; wrongful imprisonment multiplied; occasional leniency edicts could not offset his harsh bent.

sentences.zh: 嘗諭輔臣：「近連歲因災異免刑，今復當刑科三覆請旨。

translations.literal: He once instructed the chief counselors: "In recent years because of calamities executions were suspended; now again the Penal Affairs Section must submit three rehearing memorials and request the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: He once told his chief counselors: "Calamities have suspended executions in recent years; now the Penal Affairs Section must again submit three rehearings.

sentences.zh: 朕思死刑重事，欲將盜陵殿等物及毆罵父母大傷倫理者取決，餘令法司再理，與卿共論，慎之慎之。」

translations.literal: I think the death penalty is a weighty matter; I wish to take for immediate execution those who robbed tombs and palace halls and those who beat and reviled parents, greatly injuring human relations; the rest let the judicial offices reconsider and discuss jointly with you—be careful, be careful.
translations.idiomatic: I consider death a weighty matter. I wish to execute immediately those who rob tombs or palace halls and those who gravely violate family ethics; let the courts reconsider the rest jointly with you—be careful.

sentences.zh: 時以為得大體。

translations.literal: At the time this was thought to grasp the larger principle.
translations.idiomatic: At the time this was praised as grasping the larger principle.

sentences.zh: 越數年，大理寺奉詔讞奏獄囚應減死者。

translations.literal: Several years later, the Court of Judicial Review, receiving an edict, deliberated and memorialized prisoners due for reduction from death.
translations.idiomatic: Years later the Court of Judicial Review, by edict, reported prisoners eligible for commutation from death.

sentences.zh: 帝謂諸囚罪皆不赦，乃假借恩例縱奸壞法，黜降寺丞以下有差。

translations.literal: The emperor said the crimes of all prisoners were unpardonable; they falsely borrowed grace examples to release the wicked and corrupt law; court directors and below were demoted with differences in degree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor declared all their crimes unpardonable and accused the court of using grace to release the wicked; directors and below were demoted.

sentences.zh: 自九年舉秋謝醮免決囚，自後或因祥瑞，或因郊祀大報，停刑之典每歲舉行。

translations.literal: From the ninth year, autumn thanksgiving and ritual amnesty exempted executions; thereafter, whether because of auspicious omens or great suburban sacrifice and report, the rite of suspended execution was held each year.
translations.idiomatic: From the ninth year, autumn thanksgiving amnesties suspended executions; thereafter auspicious omens or great suburban rites brought annual suspension of execution.

sentences.zh: 然屢譴怒執法官，以為不時請旨，至上迫冬至，廢義而市恩也。

translations.literal: Yet he repeatedly rebuked in anger the officials holding law, saying they did not timely request the imperial will; at the extreme he pressed until the winter solstice, abandoning righteousness to buy favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he repeatedly rebuked judges for failing to seek his approval in time; at worst he delayed until the winter solstice, trading justice for favor.

sentences.zh: 遂削刑部尚書吳山職，降調刑科給事中劉三畏等。

translations.literal: Thereupon Minister of Punishment Wu Shan was stripped of office, and Supervising Secretary Liu Sanwei of the Penal Affairs Section and others were demoted and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wu Shan was stripped of office, and Penal Affairs Supervising Secretary Liu Sanwei and others were demoted.

sentences.zh: 中年益肆誅戮，自宰輔夏言不免。

translations.literal: In mid-reign he increasingly indulged in executions; even chief counselor Xia Yan did not escape.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-reign he executed ever more freely; even Chief Counselor Xia Yan was not spared.

sentences.zh: 至三十七年，乃出手諭，言：「司牧者未盡得人，任情作威。

translations.literal: By the thirty-seventh year he issued a hand instruction, saying: "Those who govern the people have not fully obtained the right men and act willfully as tyrants.
translations.idiomatic: By the thirty-seventh year he issued a hand instruction: "Local officials have not all been well chosen, and many act as tyrants.

sentences.zh: 湖廣幼民吳一魁二命枉刑，母又就捕，情迫無控，萬里叩閽。

translations.literal: The young commoner Wu Yikui of Huguang suffered wrongful punishment costing two lives; his mother was again arrested; driven to desperation with no recourse, he traveled ten thousand li to beat the appeal drum.
translations.idiomatic: Young Wu Yikui of Huguang suffered wrongful punishment costing two lives; when his mother was arrested too, he traveled ten thousand li to beat the appeal drum.

sentences.zh: 以此推之，冤抑者不知其幾。

translations.literal: Extending from this, those wrongfully suppressed—who knows how many?
translations.idiomatic: By that measure, who knows how many others suffered wrongful suppression?

sentences.zh: 爾等宜亟體朕心，加意矜恤。

translations.literal: You should urgently embody my heart and add care in compassionate treatment.
translations.idiomatic: You must urgently share my concern and show greater mercy.

sentences.zh: 仍通行天下，咸使喻之。」

translations.literal: Still extend it throughout the realm and make all understand.
translations.idiomatic: Extend this throughout the realm and make everyone understand.

sentences.zh: 是詔也，恤恤乎有哀痛之思焉。

translations.literal: This edict—how full of anxious, grieving thought.
translations.idiomatic: That edict breathed anxious, grieving concern.

sentences.zh: 末年，主事海瑞上書觸忤，刑部當以死。

translations.literal: In his late years, Chief Clerk Hai Rui submitted a memorial that gave offense; the Ministry of Punishment proposed death.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the reign, Chief Clerk Hai Rui submitted an offensive memorial; the Ministry of Punishment proposed death.

sentences.zh: 帝持其章不下，瑞得長系。

translations.literal: The emperor held his memorial and did not issue it downward; Rui was long imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kept the memorial and did not act; Hai Rui remained imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，徐階緣帝意為遺詔，盡還諸逐臣，優恤死亡，縱釋幽系。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong acceded, Xu Jie, following the emperor's intent in the testamentary edict, wholly restored all banished officials, generously treated the dead, and released those secretly imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong acceded, Xu Jie's testamentary edict restored banished officials, compensated the dead, and freed secret prisoners.

sentences.zh: 讀詔書者無不歎息。

translations.literal: Those who read the edict none did not sigh.
translations.idiomatic: All who read the edict sighed.

sentences.zh: 萬曆初，冬月，詔停刑者三矣。

translations.literal: In early Wanli, in the winter month, edicts suspending execution were already three.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wanli, three edicts had already suspended winter executions.

sentences.zh: 五年九月，司禮太監孫得勝復傳旨：「奉聖母諭，大婚期近，命閣臣於三覆奏本，擬旨免刑。」

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifth year, Director of Ceremonies Sun Desheng again transmitted the order: "Following the empress dowager's instruction, the great wedding is near; order the chief counselors on the three rehearing memorials to draft an edict exempting execution.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Wanli 5, Director Sun Desheng relayed the empress dowager's order: "The great wedding is near; draft an edict on the three rehearing memorials to suspend execution.

sentences.zh: 張居正言：「祖宗舊制，凡犯死罪鞫問既明，依律棄市。

translations.literal: Zhang Juzheng said: "The ancestral founders' old system—whenever those who committed death crimes had been clearly interrogated, they were abandoned in the market according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng replied: "Under ancestral law, once a capital crime was clearly proved, the convict was executed in the market.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖末年，世宗皇帝因齋醮，始有暫免不決之令，或間從御筆所勾，量行取決。

translations.literal: In the late years of Jiajing, Emperor Shizong because of fasting and ritual offerings first had the temporary order of exemption without decision; sometimes intermittently from the emperor's brush those marked were selected for execution.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jiajing, the emperor began temporary stays of execution for fasting and ritual offerings; sometimes he marked names for execution by his own brush.

sentences.zh: 此特近年姑息之弊，非舊制也。

translations.literal: This is especially the indulgent abuse of recent years—not the old system.
translations.idiomatic: That was a recent indulgence—not ancestral practice.

sentences.zh: 臣等詳閱諸囚罪狀，皆滅絕天理，敗傷彝倫，聖母獨見犯罪者身被誅戮之可憫，而不知彼所戕害者皆含冤蓄憤於幽冥之中，使不一雪其痛，怨恨之氣，上幹天和，所傷必多。

translations.literal: Your servants have carefully reviewed the crimes of the prisoners—all extinguished Heaven's principle and violated human relations; the empress dowager alone sees the pity of criminals personally suffering execution, yet does not know those they harmed all harbor grievance and rage in the dark; if their pain is not once cleared, resentful qi ascends and harms heavenly harmony—the harm must be many.
translations.idiomatic: We have reviewed these prisoners' crimes—they violated Heaven's principle and human relations. The empress dowager pities the condemned, but not the victims who harbor grievance in the dark; uncleared pain breeds resentment that harms heavenly harmony.

sentences.zh: 今不行刑，年復一年，充滿囹圄，既費關防，又乖國典，其於政體又大謬也。」

translations.literal: If execution is not carried out, year after year the prisons fill; it wastes guard costs and violates state precedent—greatly mistaken in governmental principle as well.
translations.idiomatic: If executions stop, prisons fill year after year, guard costs rise, and state precedent is violated—a grave error in governance.

sentences.zh: 給事中嚴用和等亦以為言。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Yan Yonghe and others also spoke thus.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretaries Yan Yonghe and others agreed.

sentences.zh: 詔許之。

translations.literal: An edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved execution.

sentences.zh: 十二年，御史屠叔明請釋革除忠臣外親。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Censor Tu Shuming requested release of the outer kin of loyal ministers eliminated in the Jianwen reign.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, Censor Tu Shuming asked to release the outer kin of Jianwen loyalists.

sentences.zh: 命自齊、黃外，方孝孺等連及者俱勘豁。

translations.literal: An order provided that apart from Qi and Huang, those implicated with Fang Xiaoru and others were all investigated and exempted.
translations.idiomatic: An order exempted all implicated with Fang Xiaoru and others except Qi and Huang.

sentences.zh: 帝性仁柔，而獨惡言者。

translations.literal: The emperor's nature was benevolent and mild, yet he alone hated those who spoke.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was gentle by nature yet hated critics.

sentences.zh: 自十二年至三十四年，內外官杖戍為民者至百四十人。

translations.literal: From the twelfth year to the thirty-fourth year, inner and outer officials beaten and banished as commoners reached one hundred forty persons.
translations.idiomatic: From year 12 to year 34, 140 officials inside and outside the capital were beaten and banished.

sentences.zh: 後不復視朝，刑辟罕用，死囚屢停免去。

translations.literal: Later he no longer held court; penal provisions were rarely used; death-row prisoners were repeatedly suspended and exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Later he stopped holding court; punishments were rarely used; death sentences were repeatedly suspended.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，酷刑多，別見，不具論。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi period cruel punishments were many; treated separately elsewhere, not fully discussed here.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi cruel punishments were many; they are treated elsewhere and not discussed here.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝即位，誅魏忠賢。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuanglie acceded, he executed Wei Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen emperor acceded, he executed Wei Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年，欽定逆案凡六等，天下稱快。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen, the ordained roster of the treason case totaled six grades; all under Heaven rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 2, the ordained Treason Case roster of six grades was published; the realm rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 然是時承神宗廢弛、熹宗昏亂之後，銳意綜理，用刑頗急，大臣多下獄者矣。

translations.literal: Yet at this time, inheriting after Shenzong's laxity and Xizong's benighted disorder, he keenly wished to put affairs in order and used punishment rather urgently; many great ministers were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yet inheriting the laxity of Wanli and the chaos of Tianqi, he tried to restore order through harsh law; many senior ministers landed in prison.

sentences.zh: 六年冬論囚，素服禦建極殿，召閣臣商榷，而溫體仁無所平反。

translations.literal: In the sixth winter, deliberating prisoners, he wore plain clothes and held court at the Jianji Hall, summoning chief counselors for consultation; yet Wen Tiren had nothing to reverse.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth winter he wore plain clothes at the Jianji Hall to review prisoners with his chief counselors, yet Wen Tiren found no case to overturn.

sentences.zh: 陝西華亭知縣徐兆麒抵任七日，城陷，坐死。

translations.literal: Xu Zhaoqi, magistrate of Huating in Shaanxi, had been in office seven days when the city fell; he was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhaoqi, magistrate of Huating in Shaanxi, had been in office only seven days when the city fell; he was condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 帝心憫之，體仁不為救。

translations.literal: The emperor in his heart pitied him, yet Tiren did not save him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pitied him, but Wen Tiren did not intervene.

sentences.zh: 十一年，南通政徐石麒疏救鄭三俊，因言：「皇上御極以來，諸臣麗丹書者幾千，圜扉為滿。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Southern Administration Vice Commissioner Xu Shilin memorialized to save Zheng Sanjun, and further said: "Since Your Majesty acceded, officials marked in red registers number nearly several thousand; the round prison is full.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, Vice Commissioner Xu Shilin petitioned to save Zheng Sanjun, saying: "Since Your Majesty acceded, nearly several thousand officials have been marked for punishment; the prisons are full.

sentences.zh: 使情法盡協，猶屬可憐，況怵惕於威嚴之下者。

translations.literal: If circumstances and law were wholly in accord, it would still be pitiable—how much more those trembling under awe and severity.
translations.idiomatic: Even when law and facts align, the toll is pitiable—how much more those living in fear under harsh rule.

sentences.zh: 有將順而無挽回，有揣摩而無補救，株連蔓引，九死一生，豈聖人惟刑之恤之意哉！」

translations.literal: There is compliance but no reversal, there is guessing but no remedy; implicating and extending branches, nine deaths and one life—how is this the intent of the sage's sparing of punishment!"
translations.idiomatic: Ministers comply but do not remonstrate, guess but do not rescue; guilt spreads by association, and men survive one death in nine—this is not the sage's merciful use of punishment!"

sentences.zh: 帝不能納也。

translations.literal: The emperor could not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not accept the plea.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，以彗見，停刑。

translations.literal: That winter, because a comet appeared, execution was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: That winter a comet appeared and executions were suspended.

sentences.zh: 其事關封疆及錢糧剿寇者，詔刑部五日具獄。

translations.literal: Matters concerning the frontier and grain funds and bandit suppression—an edict ordered the Ministry of Punishment to complete cases within five days.
translations.idiomatic: For cases involving the frontier, grain funds, or bandit suppression, an edict required the Ministry of Punishment to finish reports within five days.

sentences.zh: 十二年，御史魏景琦論囚西市，御史高欽舜、工部郎中胡璉等十五人將斬，忽中官本清銜命馳免，因釋十一人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Censor Wei Jingqi decided prisoners at the Western Market; Censor Gao Qinshun, Ministry Bureau Director Hu Lian, and fifteen others were about to be decapitated when suddenly eunuch Ben Qing, bearing an order, galloped to exempt them, and eleven were released.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, Censor Wei Jingqi reviewed prisoners at the Western Market. Fifteen men including Censor Gao Qinshun and Bureau Director Hu Lian were about to be executed when eunuch Ben Qing galloped in with an order and eleven were released.

sentences.zh: 明日，景琦回奏，被責下錦衣獄。

translations.literal: The next day Jingqi returned and memorialized; he was rebuked and sent down to the Embroidered Uniform Guard prison.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Wei Jingqi reported back and was rebuked and sent to the Embroidered Uniform Guard prison.

sentences.zh: 蓋帝以囚有聲冤者，停刑請旨，而景琦倉卒不辨，故獲罪。

translations.literal: The emperor, because prisoners had cried out injustice, had suspended execution and requested the imperial will; yet Jingqi in haste did not distinguish and therefore received guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had halted execution because prisoners cried injustice and awaited his order; Wei Jingqi acted too hastily to discern this and was punished.

sentences.zh: 十四年，大學士範復粹疏請清獄，言：「獄中文武累臣至百四十有奇，大可痛。」

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Grand Secretary Fan Fucui memorialized requesting clearing the prisons, saying: "Civil and military officials accumulated in the prisons reach more than one hundred forty—greatly painful."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, Grand Secretary Fan Fucui asked to clear the prisons, saying: "More than 140 civil and military officials languish in custody—a grievous toll."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No answer was returned.
translations.idiomatic: He received no reply.

sentences.zh: 是時國事日棘，惟用重法以繩羣臣，救過不暇，而卒無救於亂亡也。

translations.literal: At this time state affairs grew daily more urgent; he used only heavy law to bind the multitude of officials, too busy correcting faults to save them, yet in the end it could not save from chaotic ruin.
translations.idiomatic: By then the state grew daily more desperate. The emperor bound his ministers with harsh law, too busy punishing faults to govern, and in the end law could not save the dynasty from collapse.
